News.title: Remains of missing Brit found in French well 25 YEARS after his disappearance – as partner placed under investigation
News.content:
BODY IN THE WELL

BODY IN THE WELL Remains of missing Brit found in French well 25 YEARS after his disappearance – as partner placed under investigation

THE remains of a missing Brit have reportedly been found in a well more than 25 years after he disappeared in Brittany.

Anthony Rickard’s skeleton was found on May 19 at the home he had shared with his partner, Heather Comins.



She has now been put behind bars as cops launch a formal investigation into Anthony’s death – she is suspected of his murder.

The Brit dad had moved to France with Heather and their two kids in 2001.



But soon after making the move across the channel Anthony disappeared completely.

Mary Rickard, his daughter from a previous relationship, has been searching for her dad ever since.



She reported him missing at the time, but her stepmother Heather claimed he had simply left home with no explanation.

Mary said she had known the couple was “going through a rough patch”.

She claimed that Heather and Anthony’s son – her half-brother – had made a shocking confession.

Mary told prosecutors in December that he claimed Heather had admitted killing Anthony because he was “an alcoholic and violent”.



She said Heather had told her half brother about her alleged crime when he was 12 years old.

Anthony had allegedly pointed a gun at Heather, before she turned it on him.

The son allegedly told Mary that she then “left the body in her room for three days”.

He claimed Heather then hid the body in the well.

It was reportedly found buried “32 to 49ft” deep in the well earlier this week, 25 years after Anthony’s disappearance.



Investigators said the DNA matched showed that the skeleton was a parental relation to Mary and that its leg had a pin in that matched one in Anthony’s.

Heather requested bail on the grounds that she worked at an industrial bakery.

She said she “never returns to England” and is not a flight risk.

But she was kept in police custody without bail as cops question her about her partner’s mysterious death.

Anthony’s daughter Mary, who had written to French authorities last year, shared jubilant reaction on social media, saying: “Justice will be served!!!”



She added an emotional tribute to her dad, writing: “But i will remain and always will be my fathers daughter who has now lost their dad, their best friend and that can never change!

“I will miss him everyday till the day we are reunited!”

–

News.title: Second body pulled from the sea after two men in inflatable kayaks disappeared while paddling near popular UK beach
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC FIND Second body pulled from the sea after two men in inflatable kayaks disappeared while paddling near popular UK beach

A SECOND body has been found in the search for two missing men who had last been seen heading towards a popular beach.

Connor Parfitt and Simon Wilson vanished last Tuesday evening near a Haven holiday park in Gwynedd, North Wales.



They were last seen close to the beach near Hafan-y-Mor, Pwllheli, on the Llyn Peninsula with inflatable kayaks.

On Monday, police confirmed the body of Mr Parfitt had sadly been discovered on a beach in Aberystwyth at around 12.30pm on Sunday (July 26).



Today North Wales Police confirmed the body of Mr Wilson has now been found.

A force spokesperson said: “Officers were called at around 7.20pm yesterday…to reports of a body being found in the sea near to Llwyngwril, Gwynedd.



“The man has now been identified as Simon Wilson, one of the men who we circulated as missing from Pwllheli last week.

“Simon’s family and the coroner have been informed.”

Chief Inspector Stephen Pawson added: “I share my deepest condolences with Simon’s family at this incredibly difficult time.



“This is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, including the teams involved in the searches.

“Thank you to partner agencies, volunteers and members of the public who assisted in our searches.

“We would request that both Simon and Connor’s family’s privacy are respected.”

News.title: Cops probe 4 ‘unexplained’ deaths at homeless shelter where serial killer Dexter fan lived before murdering 2 roommates
News.content:
MYSTERY DEATHS Cops probe 4 ‘unexplained’ deaths at homeless shelter where serial killer Dexter fan lived before murdering 2 roommates

THE unexplained deaths of four people who were living at a homeless shelter the same time as a Dexter fanatic serial killer are being reviewed.

The probe was launched after the sentencing of James Desborough, 40, for the murder of his two roommates at the same homeless residence.



He was found guilty of murdering the two men after he chopped up their bodies and scattered the remains by his woodland cabin.

Desborough lived at Sandy Lodge Hotel in Newquay, Cornwall, which was accommodation for people suffering with homelessness or addictions, between December 2024 and April 2025, during which time two men and two women died unexpectedly.



Detective Superintendent Rachael Bentley, head of the major crime investigation team at Devon and Cornwall Police, told journalists that the investigation into the four deaths at the hotel was “ongoing”.

She added that after “final reviews” there could be “more information in the future.”



Ms Bentley said the police had attended each of the deaths and inquiries suggested natural causes and jurisdiction passed to the Cornwall Coroner.

She continued: “As part of the investigation, a detective inspector, separate to the investigation but within major crime, did a review of those deaths, and that included commissioning some more forensic work, some CCTV, and statements.



“There are still some inquiries outstanding on those.

“They remain as unexpected deaths, but there are still some inquiries outstanding. He’s not a suspect at this time.

“We’re in conversation with His Majesty’s Coroner, but they were reviewed as part of the investigation.”

The 40-year-old dismembered his victims’ bodies in Paramoor Woods, near Sticker in Cornwall and tried to burn and bury their remains.

Desborough also stole their money and used Daniel’s cash to treat himself to a “large beef roast” after chopping him up.



When he was awaiting trial for murder, he also killed his cellmate Steven Kempster at Exeter Prison.

He was handed a life sentence after strangling Kempster to death because the monster was annoyed by his snoring.

Winchester Crown Court heard around the time of the killings, Desborough messaged a pal describing himself as “absolutely bloodthirsty real hostile fuming spitting feathers”.



The text was dated on May 30, 2025 – the date Claudio became a missing person.

Chillingly, a week earlier, Desborough had told Daniel he was a “f***ing r****d” and warned him: “Don’t take me for a mug, boy.”

They had fallen out over Daniel’s relationship with Hannah Cresswell, with whom Desborough had had an affair.

Ahmed Hossain KC, prosecuting, said parts of Daniel’s dismembered body, including his torso, legs and feet, were later found in a shallow grave.

Daniel’s DNA was discovered on an axe that was hanging from a tree nearby, jurors heard.



Claudio’s shallow grave was found 18 metres away.

Cops discovered 1,900 burnt bone fragments – belonging to Claudio – at a stream nearby.

A “piece of flesh” – also from the victim – was in the water, and a search party also found “two pieces of unburnt scapula”.

Police also seized a large number of handwritten notes in the woodland cabin, the court heard.

One said: “I know I’m a killer, ready to kill and execute any predators.”



Another included “detailed travel plans and intent to leave the UK”.

This note mentioned a “shuffle bag liner”, “bodies buried”, “new disguise”, “new burner phone” and “safe house”.

Mr Hossain said Desborough was a fan of the hit TV show Dexter – in which the lead character is a serial killer who dismembers people.

The killer told a forensic biologist involved in the woodland searches that he “particularly enjoyed the dismemberment scenes” in the show.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Desborough confessed he “lost all grip on reality” and tried to hide their bodies – insisting he only found them dead on his land and that he didn’t kill them.



He will be sentenced later today.

News.title: Teacher GUILTY of blindfolding and tying boy, 10, to her marital bed to have sex with him over four-year period
News.content:
PAEDO MISS Teacher GUILTY of blindfolding and tying boy, 10, to her marital bed to have sex with him over four-year period

A TEACHER has been found guilty of blindfolding and tying a ten-year-old boy to her bed to have sex with him over a four-year period.

Deborah Franklin, 65, blindfolded and strapped the pupil to her bed so she could sexually tickle him with a feather.



The married prep school teacher met the victim, now in his 40s, when he joined her class, aged nine.

Franklin – then aged around 30 – later became his private tutor and went on to have “countless” sexual encounters with him.



She has been found guilty of eight counts of gross indecency with a boy under 14 between 1991 and 1995 at a preparatory school in Hertfordshire.

He described “countless” encounters in which Franklin would tie him to her marital bed, blindfold him, tickle him with a feather and then have sex, the court heard.



The teacher – who was married at the time – subjected him to “repeated sexual activity”, prosecutors told a trial at St Albans Crown Court.

Jurors heard that she took her clothes off in front of the boy, kissed him, got him to touch her and performed multiple sexual acts.

Franklin, of Radlett, Hertfordshire, had denied all the charges, saying she could not remember tutoring the boy.

She was emotionless in the dock as the verdicts came back.



The defendant was remanded into custody and told by Judge Kamran Choudhry that she faces a “high possibility” of being jailed at her sentencing on October 1.

The court heard that Franklin was regularly at the complainant’s house, with his sister telling jurors of the defendant: “She was fun, she was charismatic. I thought she was cool.”

The boy viewed her as “young” and “high energy”, who “presented like a mate” and spoke about drugs, cigarettes and sex, the court heard.

Franklin was “trusted” by the family to be in the boy’s room during tutoring sessions, prosecutor Gavin Pottinger said.

But Franklin was a woman “whose boundaries were just not there”, Mr Pottinger added.



The court heard that the defendant was once seen by the complainant’s sister under the covers of her brother’s bed.

The sister told jurors that on one occasion, she found Franklin “under the covers reading a book to [the complainant]”.

She described Franklin as “fun” and “charismatic”, adding: “I thought she was cool, I liked her. She was very likeable.

“She was in the house often. She became a family friend. She came on Saturday afternoons. I saw her quite a lot.”

The sibling said her brother reported Franklin to the police after finding out she was still working at the same school in 2024.



He told the court how he was in the garage of his home when Franklin asked him: “Do you want to touch me?”

The boy continued: “She kissed me on the lips and we started to touch.”

He also claimed Franklin referred to herself as his girlfriend and warned him they had to be “cautious”.

Describing another alleged encounter, the complainant said: “She asked me to come on the bed. I think it was her marital bed.

“I remember her tying me. Tying my arms down… She had a feather. Some kind of feathery gloves and fur.



“She tickled me. I remember being strapped down to the bed and blindfolded.

“She was surprised I didn’t enjoy it. Being bound to the bed it disturbed me in my teenage life when I began to understand what it would have been for her.

“At the time, I don’t think I was terrified. I wasn’t. I don’t remember being scared. But it began to bother me when I was around 14.

“I was tied to the posts, blindfolded and she was tickling me naked and I remember her being surprised I didn’t enjoy it. Her kind of quizzing me why I didn’t enjoy it, what I didn’t like.

“I was there for some hours. I remember us coming back to it later and having sex on her bed.”



A former school friend told jurors Franklin and the boy had a “very close” and “flirtatious” relationship and would hold hands on school trips.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Another friend said the pair would sit “very close” to each other when watching television.

The court was told Franklin branded the allegations as a “lot of rubbish” following her arrest.

News.title: Horror moment Virgin Mary statue is set ON FIRE at world famous Catholic shrine as vandal scrawls ‘Devil in a skirt’
News.content:
THIS is the horror moment a statue of the Virgin Mary is set on fire inside a world famous Catholic church.

The words “Devil in a skirt” had been scrawled across the base of another religious shrine outside, with police launching a manhunt for the suspected arsonist and vandal.



Bosnian police arrested a suspect on Tuesday in connection with the overnight attack on the church.

Police first received reports of vandalism to the Shrine of Our Lady statue in Medjugorje at around 4.30am, according to Vatican News.



The face and hands of the shrine that sat on top of Apparition Hill were defaced with black paint.

The pedestal at the bottom of the statue was also spray-painted with the English phrase “Devil in a skirt”.

A huge fire was also sparked inside St. James Church, according to local reports.

Surveillance footage appeared to show a man pouring gasoline onto the altar before setting it ablaze.



The two attacks came just days before Medjugorje’s annual youth prayer festival which draws in more than 50,000 pilgrims from around the world.

In a statement, the Medjugorje Parish Office condemned the vandalism but urged Catholics not to respond “with evil”.

They instead called for “prayer, fasting, and forgiveness”.



The parish added: “It is with great sadness that we received the news of the act of vandalism.

“The affected areas are being cleaned and restored as quickly as possible.

“We pray for the conversion of the hearts of those who committed this act.”

The Virgin Mary is honored with a shrine in Medjugorje where the mother of Jesus is hailed as the “Queen of Peace”.

It sits 85 miles southwest of the Bosnian capital of Sarajevo and became one of the world’s best-known Catholic pilgrimage destinations in 1981 after six children reported seeing apparitions of the Virgin Mary.



Local Ivan Dragićević, who for 50 years has claimed to have seen the mother of Jesus every day, said: “Madonna has been inviting us for decades to peace, to conversion, and to prayer.

“That is why even today we must not allow hatred to generate new hatred.”

He added while speaking to Net.hr: “What comes from God cannot be defeated by human wickedness.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“May this event be an incentive to open our hearts even more to Christ.”

Despite the attacks, officials say the shrine will always remain open.

News.title: Pedestrian killed after being hit by six vehicles including marked cop car on major A-road
News.content:
TRAGIC SMASH Pedestrian killed after being hit by six vehicles including marked cop car on major A-road

A PEDESTRIAN has died after six cars including a police vehicle drove over them.

Cops rushed to the scene after reports of a person on the carriageway.

As they scrambled to the A40 in Wales, five cars hit the person, who tragically died.

One police car also ran over the pedestrian as it arrived.





The tragedy unfolded on the A40 between the PC World roundabout and Abergwili roundabout, near Carmarthen, at 9.50pm last night.

Cops said: “Dyfed-Powys Police is investigating a six-vehicle road traffic collision, which occurred on the A40 between the PC World roundabout and Abergwili roundabout at approximately 9.50pm on Tuesday (28/7).

“The force initially received a report regarding the concern for the safety of a pedestrian who was seen to be on the carriageway.

“Following officers being deployed, further reports then indicated that several vehicles had collided with the pedestrian prior to officers’ arrival.



“A marked police vehicle was also reported to have collided with the pedestrian after arriving.

“Tragically the pedestrian was pronounced dead at the scene. Enquiries to identify them and their next of kin are now underway.

“Both carriageways of the road are likely to remain closed for a lengthy period of time today while officers remain at the scene. We would therefore ask motorists to please avoid the area and find alternative routes.

“No arrests have been made in connection with this incident.”



A mandatory referral to the Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) has been made.

Cops would like to speak to anyone with information as well as motorists who were travelling along the A40 at the time, in particular anyone with dash cam in their vehicles.

News.title: Boy, 7, dies in hospital after teen, 15, & her mum, 42, killed when ‘tide swept family away’ as they swam at beach
News.content:
A SEVEN-year-old boy has died in hospital after his teen cousin and her mum were killed when the tide reportedly swept them away.

Shelina Rahman, 41, and her daughter Sameeha Rahman, 15, were on a family day trip to the beach when they got into difficulty in the water.



They were among a group of five relatives caught up in the horror at West Mersea, near Colchester, in Essex, on the evening of July 22.

It is understood that the mother and daughter sprang into action in an effort to save the seven-year-old from the tide when they got into difficulty themselves.



The seven-year-old – who was flown to hospital in a coma – has now died, despite the best efforts of medics, Essex Police confirmed today.

In a statement, the boy’s family said: “We would also like to thank the Royal London Hospital intensive care unit team of doctors and nurses who demonstrated outstanding care and dignity for whilst we have been at the hospital.

“We would also like to thank the whole community for their support and prayers.

“We would appreciate privacy during this very difficult time.”



The dad of the daughter and wife, Dr Mansur Rahman, 49, previously told The Sun he was still suffering from shock and is “fighting to overcome” the tragedy.

He added: “I lost my daughter I lost my wife. Please pray for them.”

A source told The Sun how the grandmother of Sameeha watched her get dragged out by the tide.

They said: “The grandmother watched as she lost her daughter and her granddaughter in front of her eyes.

“She was completely helpless. She has not stopped crying since it happened.”



Witnesses also described how a young child got in trouble while playing with an inflatable close to a sandbank.

Locals said the tide came in “very quickly” before disaster struck on the packed out beach.

Cops and coastguard crews were scrambled to Sea View Holiday Park at around 5.30pm, with a seven-year-old reportedly in a coma after being rushed to hospital.

The 41-year-old mum and her teen daughter reportedly entered the water to save the youngster before the “nightmare” unfolded.

Craig Bowe, who was on a day-trip for his daughter’s 10th birthday, had dived into the sea to rescue them after he saw bodies facedown in the waves.



An eyewitness said: “The tide was a lot further in than it is now and that sandbank, they were on there and the tide came in.

“You have to be careful. It comes in very quickly. That was quite alarming, for a small place like this, I think that’s why so many people are shocked.”

Another added: “There are dangerous rip tides here and it looked like the people in trouble were on the sandbank. The water comes in so fast.



“Lots of people ran to help. It was awful, I am still traumatised by it. Everyone did what they could.

“It was like a nightmare on what had be a wonderful day. People were shouting and crying. It was just horrendous.”

Local retiree Stephen Vince, 74, said: “Everyone is so shocked. We have been pushing the council for better safety measures here for years.

“Another person died here two or three years ago. He went to rescue his son. The man survived but he drowned.



“Even before then we tried to get swimming rafts to keep people safer and towards the shore.”

The investigation is being led by Detective Chief Inspector Al Pitcher, who said: “All our thoughts are with the family and friends of those involved – as has been the case since this incident took place last week.

“Their bravery and strength has been humbling.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We continue to build a complete picture of the circumstances which led up to this incident and our work is continuing alongside our partners.”



Essex Police have asked anyone who was in the area at the time and has information or footage which could assist their investigation to contact them on 101 and quote incident 1090 of 22 July.

News.title: What does drought actually mean? The definition explained and where in the UK it has been declared
News.content:
WITH millions of households already facing hosepipe bans, environmental authorities have declared drought status in large parts of the UK.

Here is everything you need to know about what a drought actually means, who gets to decide it, and if restrictions apply.



What does drought actually mean in the UK?

In simple terms, a drought occurs when a prolonged period of low rainfall creates a severe shortage of water affecting public supplies, farming, or nature.

The last major drought declarations happened last year in August 2025, when parts of South East Wales and multiple regions in England were placed under drought status.



Which criteria have to be met?

Official drought status can only be triggered by the UK’s regional environmental watchdogs.

These are the Environment Agency in England (advised by the National Drought Group), Natural Resources Wales in Wales, SEPA in Scotland, and NIEA in Northern Ireland.



Unlike a heatwave – declared when an area tops a certain temperature threshold for three consecutive days – there is no single trigger to officially declare a drought.

Agencies instead track key indicators like rainfall totals compared to monthly averages, river flows, reservoir capacities, and the frequency of wildfires.

When a combination of these factors shows that the local environment is under severe stress, the watchdog officially moves an area from “prolonged dry weather” into “drought” status.

Does it mean any new rules or restrictions?

An official drought declaration by an environmental agency does not automatically trigger mandatory rules or turned-off taps for households.



But the public is urged to save water to take pressure off local water sources.

You are also advised to avoid open flames, BBQs, or campfires in dry countryside areas to prevent wildfires.

Water utility companies may introduce consumer restrictions like hosepipe bans based on local reservoir stocks and consumer demand.

Where has drought been declared?

Official drought status was first declared in North Wales and the Upper Severn region earlier this month, following record-breaking dry spells and weeks without significant rain.

The Welsh zones in drought include Clwyd, Dee, North and South Gwynedd, Upper Severn, and Ynys Mon (Anglesey).



Parts of north Wales have received less than 2% of their expected July rainfall, with many locations seeing no significant rain since July 6.

In England, seven areas of central, eastern and southern England are now officially in drought following record low rain and high temperatures, the Environment Agency has said.

Devon and Cornwall

East Anglia

Hampshire and the Isle of Wight

Hertfordshire and the whole of London

Thames Valley

The West Midlands

Wessex (covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and south Gloucestershire)

Multiple hosepipe bans are already in place, impacting 23million customers.

News.title: Abusive husband given chance to change then murders wife by knifing her 40 times
News.content:
Abusive husband given chance to change then murders wife by knifing her 40 times

Syed Ahmad, 45, brutally attacked Anam Rafay at their home in Wythenshawe on the morning of January 27 this year

View 3 Images Syed Ahmad has admitted murdering his wife Anam Rafay (Image: Manchester Police)

An abusive and controlling husband stabbed his wife to death in a frenzied attack after she gave him one final chance to change his ways.

‌



Syed Ahmad, 45, savagely attacked Anam Rafay at their home in Wythenshawe, Greater Manchester, on the morning of January 27 this year.

‌



A post mortem revealed Mrs Rafay suffered 40 stab wounds to her neck, body, arms and legs and died as a result of a cardiac arrest, the MEN reports.

‌



During a trial at Manchester Crown Court, Ahmad denied murder, claiming he did not intend to kill her and was suffering from 'abnormal mental functioning' at the time.

While giving evidence, he said that he 'heard a voice which told him his wife was going to smash his head in', before asserting that he acted in self-defence. After two weeks of the trial, Ahmad pleaded guilty to murder. He is due to be sentenced on Friday (July 31).

View 3 Images Police at the scene of the stabbing in Wythenshawe (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

‌



Police probe four 'unexplained' deaths where killer Dexter fan lived before murdering roommates READ MORE :

Bill Baker KC, prosecuting, said Ahmad and Mrs Rafay were married by way of arranged marriage in Pakistan in 2005 when she was 16 and he was 25.

She had previously lived in Pakistan with her family while Ahmad lived in the UK with his family after relocating there as a child.

"The defendant's family promised her family that she would be treated as an actual daughter, not daughter in law. They didn't do so," Mr Baker said. "They made her do all the housework and she wasn't allowed to eat until they had finished eating."

‌



Ahmad was described as being "abusive, controlling and violent throughout their marriage". A former colleague of Mrs Rafay, who worked alongside her at a Manchester school from 2019, said Ahmad would make his wife feel 'uncomfortable' and controlled her finances.

Describing his "strange behaviour", Gemma Mulvaney said: "He used to follow her to work in the car, but she would walk. I call it kerb crawling. He used to drive really slowly next to her.

"He would then wait until she entered the building and then he would leave. I asked her why he doesn't let her in the car and she said she didn't know."

‌



Another former colleague, Kirsty Tomlin, said Mrs Rafay had previously described Ahmad as "horrible" and "evil". "She said he used to beat her up, he never helped her in the house. He just wasn't nice to her," she said.

View 3 Images Police guard the scene after the attack on Lulworth Gardens (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

"She said she wasn't happy in her marriage. She said she couldn't leave him because he would kill her."

‌



Manchester Crown Court heard that in June last year, Mrs Rafay began speaking to a man she had met on TikTok.

The pair grew close, embarked on trips into the city together, and Mrs Rafay went on to "fall in love with him and wanted to marry him". In September last year she reached out to a mufti, also known as a divorce mediator, in Longsight to enquire about obtaining a divorce application.

The following October she served that application upon Ahmad who requested mediation. She agreed to give him "one more chance to change", but tragically never did, the court heard.

‌



The night before the alleged attack, Mrs Rafay told Ahmad that she wanted a divorce. On the morning of January 27 this year, Mrs Rafay was filling up a water bottle in the kitchen when Mr Ahmad entered from behind, armed with a kitchen knife.

He then repeatedly stabbed her, causing her to collapse to the kitchen floor, where he continued the brutal assault.

"She managed to get up and went next door seeking help. The defendant chased her, caught up with her and started stabbing her again," Mr Baker said.

‌



Neighbours watched in horror as Ahmad stabbed her on the ground before he was seen 'walking back to the house leaving her dead or dying'. The prosecutor stated that as the defendant made his way back to the house, he was seen to 'smile or smirk'.

Ahmad then sent a message to the family WhatsApp group, and to Mrs Rafay's dad, which read: "I have killed my wife." In arrest footage shown to the court, Ahmad said: "I'm truly sorry, I'm truly sorry, I'm sorry."

He was later heard to say: "Self defence, self defence, she attacked me." While giving evidence, his barrister, Mark Ford KC, asked him: "Do you accept you killed your wife?".

Article continues below

"I was in a psychotic episode," Ahmad said. He then claimed he "heard visuals and sounds" of a male voice telling him his wife would "smash his head in".

"Do you have any memory of stabbing your wife?" Mr Ford asked. "No. Just flashbacks. Someone stabbed my wife, I think it was me," Ahmad said.

Ahmad, of Lulworth Gardens, Wythenshawe, denied murder and an alternate offence of manslaughter. Having finished giving evidence on Tuesday, July 28, Ahmad pleaded guilty to murder, with jurors asked to formally record a guilty verdict. He is due to be sentenced on Friday, July 31.

News.title: 'Use less water' alert as drought declared in half of England - water saving tips
News.content:
'Use less water' alert as drought declared in half of England - water saving tips

Small steps, such as turning off the taps when brushing teeth, can help

View 3 Images Water saving tips as hot weather continues (Image: Getty)

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and Environment Agency have today, July 29, declared that half of England is facing a drought. Seven areas of England are now officially in drought after record low rainfall and exceptionally high temperatures.

‌



The government has said that river levels in affected areas are very low and that crops are being picked early. There is also a greater risk of wildfires. Millions of people are being urged to follow restrictions and use "a little less water" where possible. The government says it is closely monitoring water levels and limiting how much water people can take from rivers.

‌



This is the third drought the UK has had in five years, with droughts also declared in 2022 and 2025. The seven areas in drought are:

‌



East Anglia Hertfordshire and the whole of London Thames Valley Hampshire and the Isle of Wight Devon and Cornwall The West Midland Wessex (covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and south Gloucestershire)

Helen Wakeham, Director of Water at the Environment Agency and Chair of the National Drought Group, said: "The hot and dry weather means we are currently using water faster than nature can replenish it. A second consecutive summer drought is an exceptionally serious situation and one that will have long-lasting impacts on our environment, wildlife, and the economy. We want everyone to stay safe and hydrated during the hot weather but every drop we can save is a drop more for nature and agriculture."

Following a very wet winter this year, the UK went on to face a very dry summer. Most of the rain expected in July never fell. Many parts of southern England have seen almost no rain at all. The hot weather is drying up the water in the ground. According to the Met Office, more heatwaves are coming, and there is no rain in the forecast.

‌



View 3 Images The River Thames, where water levels have dropped due to prevailing hot and dry weather conditions

Met Office Chief Meteorologist, Will Lang, said: "The warm and exceptionally dry conditions experienced across much of England over recent months are continuing to have a significant impact. Many areas have received very little or no rainfall throughout July, extending a period of below-average rainfall that has persisted across parts of the country since spring.

"While there are indications of occasional unsettled spells during the first part of August, bringing the chance of rain to some locations, there is currently little sign of the widespread, sustained rainfall that would be needed to make a significant difference to the areas most affected by the dry weather. The Met Office continues to work closely with the Environment Agency and partners across the water sector, providing expert meteorological information and forecasts to support drought monitoring, planning and response activities."

‌



Alongside seven areas in drought, these areas are now in prolonged dry weather:

Kent and East Sussex

Cumbria and Lancashire

Greater Manchester, Merseyside and Cheshire

East Midlands

Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire

The rest of Solent and the South Downs

Just Yorkshire and the North East remain in normal status, with the situation under close review.

‌



A statement on Gov.uk reads: "With everyone’s help in using a little less water and following restrictions, our current reserves should be enough for the coming months until the next period of sustained rainfall. Small steps, such as turning off the taps when brushing teeth or shaving, taking a shorter shower or fixing a leaking toilet can really add up."

View 3 Images The high temperatures and dry conditions have led to scorched greenery

How to save water at home

There are many ways that you can save water around your home. According to the Water Services Regulation Authority (Ofwat), these tips may be helpful:

‌



Use a bowl in the sink when washing fruit, vegetables, or dishes. You can then use the wastewater to water your plants. Fill a jug of water and put it in the fridge for when you want a cool drink. Turn off the tap when you clean your teeth. A running tap uses up to nine litres of water a minute.

Wait until you have a full load before using your washing machine or your dishwasher. Some new washing machines use less than seven litres of water per kilogram of clothes, while modern dishwashers use as little as 10-15 litres per cycle.

If possible, take a shower instead of a bath. A five-minute shower uses about 40 litres of water. This is about half the volume of a standard bath. Use a water-saving device in your toilet cistern. Depending on the size of your cistern, you could save between one and three litres each time you flush the toilet.

Article continues below

Using a watering can in the garden instead of a sprinkler or a hosepipe. Garden sprinklers and hosepipes left running can use between 500 and 1,000 litres of water an hour.

Think about fitting a water butt to collect rainwater from your roof. Water butts usually store about 200 litres of water. In addition to being better for watering your plants, using rainwater in the garden reduces the amount of treated water you use. Check your property regularly for leaks on your internal plumbing.

News.title: France wildfires live: Astonishing arrests as 42C heatwave threatens Bordeaux
News.content:
A handful of people have been arrested for allegedly taking advantage of those affected by wildfires in south-west France, which have forced more than 220,000 people to flee

Astonishing arrests have been made as firefighters continue to battle wildfires that have ravaged 42,000 hectares of south-west France and spread into parts of the Bordeaux metropolitan area.

More than 220,000 people in the Gironde region have been evacuated over the past week in what has been France's largest peacetime evacuation.

But while many have sought refuge in evacuation centres, a handful of people have instead found themselves in police custody. A man was arrested after allegedly "posing" as a psychologist offering paid counselling sessions to those affected by the fires, French police told Sky News.

Two men were arrested several days ago on suspicion of "stealing food and supplies" intended for those affected by the wildfires, the broadcaster reported. Officers have been standing outside evacuation centres and fire-ravaged areas to keep people safe and ensure restricted zones are protected.

Although the regional prefecture said the wildfires remain "stabilised", with "several flare-ups" brought under control overnight, officials said weather conditions remain "unfavourable" today. Temperatures could climb to a scorching 42C in Bordeaux, national weather service Météo-France said.

News.title: Andy Burnham speech live: Emotional PM's THREE pledges to fix social care prioritised over assisted dying
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham is outlining how he will fix the creaking social care sector in a major speech this morning, and even invited Kemi Badenoch and Ed Davey into cross-party talks

Andy Burnham promised to fix the crisis-hit social care sector in a major speech this morning, and a new dementia tsar would be appointed.

The new Prime Minister outlined three key parts to his strategy:

Bringing forward the deadline for a review into social care Reviewing pay and career progression for care workers Working cross-party to try and find some kind of consensus

He warned the creaking system can no longer be used as a political football while the NHS and families looking after loved ones count the cost.

He invited Tory chief Kemi Badenoch and Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey to urgent talks later today to discuss the problem governments have kicked into the long-grass for decades.

Ahead of his speech, Mr Burnham said: “Politicians might have different views but I’m serious about fixing this issue and to do that, we have to find common ground and listen to others to find a way forward.”

Follow below for all the latest updates

News.title: Man who 'started fire which killed two pensioners' found dead in bin days later
News.content:
Man who 'started fire which killed two pensioners' found dead in bin days later

Paul Smith, 40, is believed to have started the fire which killed Sheila Jackson, 83, and Eric Greener, 77, in St Helens - he was found dead in a wheelie bin a week later

View 2 Images Paul Smith, 40, was found dead in a wheelie bin (Image: LIVERPOOL ECHO)

A man thought to have started a fire which killed an elderly couple was found dead in a wheelie bin a week later, an inquest heard.

‌



Paul Smith, 40, known as Smigger, is believed to have started the blaze at the home of Sheila Jackson, 83, and her partner, Eric Greener, 77, in St Helens last July.

‌



The couple were rescued from the blaze but died in hospital from burns and smoke inhalation.

‌



Smith’s body was discovered seven days after the attack, in a bin where it had been moved after he died in a bath, having taken a cocktail of drugs, an inquest heard on Wednesday.

The hearing at the Gerard Majella Courthouse in Liverpool was told police were called on July 22 by Steven Wales, who told them a man had either drowned or overdosed in the bath at a property at Coniston Street, Everton, two days earlier.

View 2 Images The cordon around the derelict building where Paul Joseph Smith was found (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



Van deliberately driven into police officers in Scotland with suspect on the loose READ MORE :

Senior coroner for Liverpool Andre Rebello said: “Merseyside Police were deployed and located a male, deceased, in a wheelie bin at the rear of derelict properties on Thirlmere Road, which backs on to Coniston Street and is separated by an alleyway.

“The deceased male was identified by police as Paul Joseph Smith.”

Mr Smith, who lived on Lower Breck Road, had last spoken to his family on July 19 and was reported missing by his brother Michael on July 21.

‌



In a report, Home Office pathologist Dr Matthew Lyall said toxicology results showed Mr Smith had taken heroin close to the time of his death, as well as a “relatively large amount of cocaine” and a number of sedatives.

Dr Lyall said drowning could not be proved or excluded.

He added: “Neither can it be entirely excluded that the deceased was held under water by a third party, but pathological findings cannot prove that occurred.”

‌



He recorded the cause of death as mixed drug toxicity.

The court heard that police were satisfied the death was not caused by criminality.

Mr Rebello said it was understood there were criminal proceedings ongoing regarding the disposal of the body.

‌



Recording the death as drug-related, the coroner said: “He died from taking illicit and and sedative drugs which caused respiratory failure.”

Earlier this year Kevin Weetman, 34, Kylie Maynard, 37, and Lee Owens, 46, were jailed for the manslaughter of Mr Greener and Ms Jackson.

A trial at Liverpool Crown Court heard that Mr Smith had travelled with Owens to the home in South John Street just after 12.30am on July 15.

Article continues below

Weetman was jailed for life with a minimum of 25 years for planning the attack after Mrs Jackson’s son George Jackson, 48, refused to sell drugs for him.

Maynard, said to be the “trusted lieutenant” in Weetman’s drugs line, was jailed for 23 years and Owens was sentenced to 13 years and six months.

News.title: Love Island final LIVE: Fans speculate on feud as finalist image emerges
News.content:
Yesterday's final of Love Island crowned Lorenzo and Julia as the 13th season's winners, with Jasmine and Kavan coming second, and Simba and Angelista in third

The Love Island has officially ended with Lorenzo Alessi and Julia Majchrzak announced as winners, beating out stiff competition from Kavan Murphy and Jasmine Muller.

However, it wasn't without drama as one Islander was noticeably absent from the proceedings, while fans were convinced that there was drama brewing between others, as an image of the finalists has emerged.

Since their win, some fans have voiced their doubts about Julia and Lorenzo's relationship, but Lorenzo has hit back at those comments, saying that he understands where they're coming from, as he and Julia have not been as quick to go through milestones on TV, but that pressure would have "ruined things" for him.

This hasn't been helped by lingering beliefs that Lorenzo and Jasmine had feelings for each tother. When Jasmine learned that the public were calling her and Lorenzo 'Jarenzo', she visibly cringed and looked horrified as she covered Kavan's ears.

News.title: Police probe four 'unexplained' deaths where killer Dexter fan lived before murdering roommates
News.content:
Police probe four 'unexplained' deaths where killer Dexter fan lived before murdering roommates

Devon and Cornwall Police are now making enquiries into the four sudden deaths at a homeless shelter in Cornwall

View Image James Desborough (Image: Devon and Cornwall Police/PA Wire)

Officers are probing four unexplained deaths at a homeless shelter in Cornwall which happened at the same time a newly-convicted murderer lived there.

Fan of TV serial killer show Dexter James Desborough, 40, has already been convicted of two killings prompting Devon and Cornwall Police to make new enquiries. Desborough lived at Sandy Lodge Hotel - a facility accommodating people experiencing homelessness or addictions - in Newquay, Cornwall.

This was happening between December 2024 and April 2025, during which time two men and two women died unexpectedly. Detective Superintendent Rachel Bentley, of Devon and Cornwall Police, said the force "don't believe there is a link at this time" but the investigation is ongoing, with "some final reviews to be done".

Det Supt Bentley said officers attended each of the four deaths and enquiries suggested natural causes. The deaths were then passed to the coroner but these investigations were paused when Desborough was arrested for murder.

The officer said: "It was quite right that those coronial investigations paused when James Desborough was arrested for murder. That’s why the major crime investigation team commenced a review and conducted some further investigation because it was right to pause.

"Now James had committed a murder, so just to review those circumstances and those final investigation inquiries are ongoing currently. I said before there’s no other information that’s come into the investigation that suggests that he’s linked to any of the deaths.

"We don’t believe we’re looking for any victims, but I do want to stress that the investigations are ongoing. They are going to be reviewed again now the trial has concluded, but at this time we are not looking at any other investigations and at this time he’s not a suspect in any other deaths."

Desborough was convicted of killing Claudio Aquilino, 57, and Daniel Coleman, 43, before hiding their bodies in Cornwall last year. The former builder is already serving a life sentence after he strangled his prison cellmate Steven Kempster at HMP Exeter while on remand awaiting his trial.

As he killed three people in separate incidents over five months, Desborough is now considered a serial killer. Both victims lived with Desborough at the homeless hostel. The last time they were both seen alive was in Desborough's company.

The two victims' bodies were dismembered in an area of Sticker Woods, near St Austell, where Desborough lived in a wooden cabin. Officers later discovered 1,900 burned bone fragments from Mr Aquilino's body at the location.

Parts of Mr Coleman's body, including his torse, legs and feet, were found in a shallow grave nearby. Desborough told a forensic biologist who was searching the woods for Mr Coleman’s body that he "particularly enjoyed the dismemberment scenes" in the television series Dexter.

Desborough, who is 5ft10in tall and weighs almost 18st, went on to spend his victims' money on drugs and alcohol.
