Sports.title: Ex-Chelsea star Marc Cucurella gets TATTOO of his Spain manager after making promise ahead of World Cup win
Sports.content:
Marc Cucurella has kept his promise to have an image of Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente tattooed on his body.

Cucurella helped Spain to World Cup glory earlier this month and had promised to honour De la Fuente in unusual style.

The former Chelsea left-back, who joined Real Madrid this summer, revealed the tribute to the 65-year-old Spain boss on the underside of his arm.

The design was revealed on Instagram on Tuesday, featuring a portrait of De la Fuente alongside the World Cup.

'Promise fulfilled,' Cucurella posted on his Instagram account alongside a picture of him having the tattoo done.

Speaking in the aftermath of their World Cup final 1-0 after extra-time victory over Argentina, De la Fuente joked that Cucurella might have made a mistake.

Marc Cucurella kept his promise of getting Spain manager Luis de la Fuente tattooed on his arm

Cucurella started in all eight of Spain's matches as they won the World Cup earlier this month

'I've already told them, 'did you make a mistake?' he joked in his post-match news conference. 'They did, but they'll enjoy it.

'I'm not so terribly ugly that they will need to put it somewhere nobody can see it. But it makes me laugh and I am proud they keep their promises.'

Real Madrid's Cucurella, who carried his wife's pyjama top with him as a lucky charm during the World Cup, started in all eight matches for Spain, helping the team keep seven clean sheets.

Sports.title: If Arsenal want to be a big club they need to prove it - signing 'good' players is no longer enough and a star must arrive or they'll be left behind by their rivals, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
If Arsenal want to be a big club they need to prove it - signing 'good' players is no longer enough and a star must arrive or they'll be left behind by their rivals, writes ISAAN KHAN

Unlock more from Isaan Khan inside the Arsenal camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Arsenal have conquered the Premier League – but now comes the challenge which could define Mikel Arteta’s reign.

After ending their 22-year league title drought and coming within a penalty shootout of being European champions, signing ‘good’ players is no longer enough. At present, Arsenal have only added Christos Tzolis (£36million) and Illan Meslier (free transfer), while making Piero Hincapie’s loan move permanent.

Of course, they are shopping in a market reserved for only a handful of elite clubs. Their ambition isn’t to solely strengthen the squad with promising talent or dependable depth.

Instead, it’s to recruit genuine superstars capable of deciding the biggest matches and turning Arsenal from one-time champions into serial winners, the likes of Vinicius Junior and Bruno Guimaraes.

But unless they succeed in the final five weeks of the transfer window, they risk being left behind at a time when their Big Six rivals have splashed the cash in a bid to knock Arsenal off their new perch.

Chelsea have spent an eye-watering £117m on Morgan Rogers, a player who was earmarked for weeks to join Arsenal but exceeded the club’s valuation. Tottenham have paid £92.5m for Sandro Tonali, along with £85m for Mateus Fernandes and £52m on Jan Paul van Hecke, with £60m Savinho next in their sights.

Arsenal have conquered the Premier League — but now comes the challenge which could define Mikel Arteta’s reign

The only new outfielder Arsenal have signed this summer is £36m Christos Tzolis from Club Bruges

Manchester City bought Elliot Anderson for £116m, while rivals United have rebuilt their midfield with Andrey Santos (£50m) and Youri Tielemans (£35m).

The coming weeks represent crunch time, and will go some way to revealing whether Arsenal truly are ready and willing to build the dynasty Arteta craves.

It will also test the proficiencies of Andrea Berta, who had a solid window last summer, signing eight players. But now the heat is on from an insatiable fanbase.

Arsenal’s ambitions, however, are not easy to realise. The feeling inside the club is that deals for star names take time, and have been complicated by a World Cup which has caused delays.

Insiders expect the coming weeks to be very busy regarding incomings.

Arsenal are pursuing Vinicius and closely monitoring the situation around his contract, which expires next June. Real Madrid are very keen to renew the Brazilian’s deal but nothing has been decided yet.

Daily Mail Sport understands Arsenal have a few high-profile left wingers on the list in case their pursuit of Vinicius fails. Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola was one, though he is closing in on a move to Liverpool.

Arsenal know they need to go big this summer, and have been looking into a deal for Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior

Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes is also on Arsenal's list this summer

Arsenal have also looked at PSG left winger Bradley Barcola if they cannot sign Vinicius, but the Frenchman now appears destined for Liverpool

If Vinicius or a player of his ilk does join Arsenal, the club are presented with circumstances they’ve not quite navigated for some time.

Ever since Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's ill-fated £350,000-a-week contract, signed after he led Arteta to his first trophy in the 2020 FA Cup final, Arsenal have been very careful with their players' wages and signing ready-made superstars.

Arteta likes control, with the Aubameyang case study – he was stripped of the captaincy and booted out of the club halfway through the three-year contract after disciplinary issues – leaving the Spaniard wary of signing big-name players who could alter the team’s balance.

It is believed Vinicius is currently paid around £247,000 to £279,000 a week after tax. To earn that amount in the UK, the Gunners would need to pay him somewhere between £450,000 and £500,000 a week.

That would make him Arsenal's highest-paid player by far and shatter the current wage structure. Bukayo Saka is Arsenal’s highest-paid player on £300,000 a week.

It could have ramifications in terms of other players demanding better deals. While the star power Vinicius brings is a further element to consider.

For all the complexities, Arsenal’s hierarchy are aware that ambition has to be matched by action. They are no longer trying to close the gap. They are ahead, and trying to stay there. That requires attracting players who already operate at the highest level and can immediately raise the team’s ceiling.

There is also an acceptance that opportunities to sign generational talents rarely come without risk. The financial commitment and the dressing room dynamics that follow all require careful consideration.

Yet whether Arsenal land the superstar signing they desire this summer may ultimately shape how this Arteta era is remembered.

Vinicius' wages would be significantly higher than any other Arsenal player's, and would risk causing disharmony in the squad

The last time Arsenal handed out a mega contract to a player it all ended in tears, with Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's deal ripped up 18 months in

Rather than chasing the established elite clubs, Arsenal are expected to behave like one. The coming weeks will reveal whether they are prepared to do that

Winning the league proved Arsenal could reach the summit, though staying there requires a different level of ruthlessness. The Gunners have won the English title 14 times but it has been more than 90 years since they retained it – winning three in a row from 1933-35.

It demands competing financially with Europe's biggest clubs and convincing the world's elite players that north London is the destination to be.

That is the challenge now facing Arteta, Berta and Arsenal's hierarchy. Rather than chasing the established elite clubs, they are expected to behave like one. The coming weeks will reveal whether Arsenal are prepared to do that.

Sports.title: Man United youngsters
Sports.content:
As opportunity knocks for a number of Manchester United’s academy stars in pre-season, only the chosen few will be part of the first-team squad once the new Premier League campaign gets underway.

United are open to the majority of the Under 21s who have featured in the opening friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg going out on loan to further their development, with the exception of players like Shea Lacey, Jack and Tyler Fletcher and rising star JJ Gabriel.

For several youngsters who have been on the first-team fringes for some time now, the move could be permanent after the club made a decision on their futures this week.

Goalkeeper Radek Vitek, left back Harry Amass and midfielders Dan Gore and Toby Collyer all spent last season out on loan and have been told they are unlikely to feature for United this season either.

In the case of Vitek and Amass, United are prepared to sell both players or consider another loan with an option to buy. Until then, both players will remain part of the first-team squad and train at Carrington.

Czech keeper Vitek, who has played more minutes than anyone against Wrexham and Rosenborg, is a target for Middlesbrough and a host of other Championship clubs after starring on loan at Bristol City last season.

Michael Carrick has given a lot of game time to his young academy stars in pre-season

A host of United youngsters got a runout in Norway, including Shea Lacey (front left), Harry Amass (centre) and 15-year-old JJ Gabriel (back right)

Amass played in both games and got a goal and an assist against Rosenborg. He is valued at around £6million after spending last season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich.

With United still in the market for a third central midfielder after paying a combined £85m to sign Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, Gore and Collyer are believed to have been told that their best hope of regular football next season will be with the Under 21s.

Hull City retain an interest in re-signing Collyer following his loan there last season, and Gore is available again after a successful loan spell at Rotherham.

There is no shortage of other United youngsters looking to impress in the remaining four pre-season games against Atletico Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds and AC Milan, even though opportunities may be harder to come by as United’s World Cup stars return to action.

The club are famed for their youth system, and a feature of United’s first two pre-season games has been how well the academy players seized their opportunity in Helsinki and Trondheim.

Lacey scored United’s opening goal over Rosenborg on Friday after he was named in the starting line-up, and Jaydan Kamason starred with two assists when Michael Carrick brought on the kids in the second half and they stretched the lead to 5-0.

United's first-team stars will be looking over their shoulder with so much talent waiting in the wings

In the first game against Wrexham, the academy side played more fluent football than the seniors who went 1-0 down before half-time, but United couldn’t find the equaliser their performance deserved.

Lacey will be looking to kick on after making his first-team breakthrough last season along with the Fletcher twins, and Gabriel is edging ever closer to a debut. Jim Thwaites is also understood to be particularly highly-rated by Carrick and his coaching staff even though he hasn’t played yet.

Here Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the exciting youngsters knocking on the first-team door.

SHEA LACEY

The only outfield player from the academy to make the starting line-up against Rosenborg, Lacey justified his inclusion with a well-taken goal just after the half-hour mark to set United on their way to a comprehensive victory.

The 19-year-old from Liverpool is predominantly a right winger but demonstrated his versatility in Trondheim by playing in the No 10 role and drifting wide to link up play.

Lacey’s star quality was underlined when Thomas Tuchel called him up to train with the England senior squad in October, and he made his first two appearances for United before being sent off on his Old Trafford debut against Brighton in the FA Cup.

He re-appeared at Brighton in the Premier League on the final day of the season, though, and we will undoubtedly be seeing more of him this term.

Lacey made four first-team appearances last season, including three in the Premier League

Lacey saw red on his Old Trafford debut in the FA Cup against Brighton for throwing the ball away in a show of dissent

JACK FLETCHER

The older of the Fletcher twins – who joined United from Manchester City for a joint fee of around £1.25m three years ago – Jack was named in the starting line-up for the Wrexham game and performed well in the No 10 role before Carrick made wholesale changes at half-time.

He and Tyler play in central midfield, but they are expected to stay at United this season despite the club’s £85m investment in Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, and plans to sign a third midfielder.

Jack is seen as a more creative player and tends to operate further forward, although the England youth international can also be used as a right winger or full back.

The 19-year-old made three first-team appearances last season and will be aiming to add more this term.

Jack Fletcher tends to operate further forward in midfield but can also be used as a right winger or full back

TYLER FLETCHER

He didn’t start against Wrexham but at least had the distinction of captaining United’s younger XI in the second half in Helsinki, before coming on as a substitute along with his brother when Carrick made changes after an hour against Rosenborg.

This could be a big season for Tyler after he made his senior international debut for Scotland in a friendly against Bolivia last month and then got a late call-up for the World Cup following an injury to Billy Gilmour.

Like Lacey, he played for United at Brighton on the last day of the season in May, and those two are understood to be at the front of the queue for first-team opportunities this year.

Tyler Fletcher had the distinction of captaining United’s younger XI in the second half in Helsinki against Wrexham

JJ GABRIEL

The most eagerly anticipated appearance in pre-season is likely to be made by the young man who doesn’t turn 16 until October.

Gabriel was included in United’s squad for the first time for the trip to Norway last week, but was one of only three players from the 25-man party not to get on the pitch.

It’s only a matter of time before the player dubbed Kid Messi gets his chance, after Premier League rules prevented United from naming him in their squad last season because he was only 14 when it began.

Gabriel still made an impression, though, as he was called up to first-team training in the autumn and starred for the Under 18s with 29 goals in 32 appearances to win the Under 18s Premier League player of the season award. Expect to hear a lot more about this boy.

JJ Gabriel has only just turned 15 but could be in line for a Premier League debut this season

JAYDAN KAMASON

The England youth international was United’s standout performer in the second half against Rosenborg, getting forward down the right flank to set up goals for Harry Amass and Ethan Williams.

Kamason struggled with injuries last season but is hoping to have more luck this term, and has certainly made a promising start in pre-season.

The 19-year-old is prepared to go out on loan to further his development, but has his sights locked firmly on a career at Old Trafford.

‘If I need a few loans or whatever, we'll have to see, but I'm trying to get to that top level – and that's Manchester United. You have to be ambitious,’ he said after the game in Trondheim.

Jaydan Kamason struggled with injuries last season but is hoping to have more luck this term, and has certainly made a promising start in pre-season

JIM THWAITES

Although he has been left on the bench for both pre-season games so far, Thwaites is said to be particularly highly regarded among the current crop of Under 21s.

A gifted midfielder and dead-ball specialist, the 18-year-old has seized his opportunity to train with the senior squad since Ruben Amorim first invited him in, and was rewarded by Carrick for his performance during the training camp in Dublin in April with a place on the bench at Chelsea.

With United strengthening in midfield, they have to make a decision about whether to keep Thwaites or send him out on loan after a planned move in January was scuppered by injury.

Jim Thwaites is a dead-ball specialist and is particularly highly regarded among the current crop of Under 21s

JACOB DEVANEY

Devaney has come off the bench to play in central defence in both pre-season games despite preferring a midfield role, and got on the scoresheet against Rosenborg with United’s third goal from a corner shortly after replacing Ayden Heaven.

The 19-year-old excelled as a midfielder on loan at St Mirren during a difficult season for the Scottish club, and is ready to head out again if it boosts his hopes of playing for United.

Jacob Devaney struck for United in their 5-0 pre-season friendly win over Rosenborg in Norway last week

‘The main aim for me is to play for Manchester United week in, week out,’ said the Republic of Ireland Under 21s international in Trondheim.

‘Obviously, I want to play first-team football. So whether that is at United, learning from the best for the next year, or if I have to go on loan again and gain more valuable experience, that's what I'll do.’

PS: Not all the young players knocking on the first-team door at United this season will have come through the club’s academy.

There is great excitement around teenage winger Tynan Thompson who has moved to Old Trafford from Tottenham in a deal worth £4m plus £4m in add-ons.

Thompson will be part of the senior group at Carrington, but the 18-year-old hasn’t trained with them yet and it’s too early to tell if he will feature in pre-season as United’s World Cup contingent continue to report back.

Sports.title: Downfall of 'Clicky Ponting': Millions across globe are outraged by obscure village cricket 'cheat' storm - now he is dropped by his sponsor
Sports.content:
Tourists swarmed on to Saltburn-by-the-Sea's pier yesterday, guzzling fish, chips and Mr Whippy ice-creams, but a few hundred yards inland, another great Victorian landmark was eerily quiet. The seaside town's historic cricket ground, with its white picket fence and neatly mown outfield, stood empty. Not a single holidaying schoolchild was using its well-tended nets or 'Arthur Heslop Indoor Training Facility'. The doors to a £600,000 lottery-funded pavilion were bolted shut. All that could be heard was an occasional seagull, venturing inland from the North Sea. And this unseasonal calm turned out to be at the centre of an utterly toxic storm. To blame is a bizarre cheating scandal which, in just a few short hours, has turned Saltburn Cricket Club from a beloved local institution, which last year celebrated its 150th birthday, into a symbol of sporting corruption which has made headlines around the world. The whole thing revolves around an incident during Saturday's match against Norton Cricket Club, in which Saltburn's second XI was seeking to cement their place atop Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League. Footage shows the match nicely poised, with Norton on 39 for 2, when its number four batsman, Noman Shabir, strode to the crease. He then played at and completely missed his first delivery, a ball from Saltburn's Sam Morrison which had pitched outside the off stump. So far, so normal. As the ball passed Shabir, however, something very strange had happened: the fielder standing at first slip clicked his fingers. This imitated the sound of the ball nicking the edge of Shabir's bat. And when the wicketkeeper then took the ball safely, the fielding side appealed for a catch. Having heard the noise, the umpire raised his finger to give Shabir out. Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it seem as though a batter had been caught behind when they hadn't hit the ball Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his actions on the cricket field The Saltburn player was seen on camera clicking his fingers each time the ball neared the bat Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out Although the batsman was clearly outraged, his attempt to explain to the elderly umpire that he hadn't actually touched the ball got short shrift. Saltburn duly went on to skittle out Norton for 143, giving them a thumping 159-run victory. There things would have ended, were it not for the fact that (in common with many recreational cricket matches in the online era) the game happened to have been live-streamed online. A recording was preserved on the English Cricket Board's 'Play Cricket' website. A Durham-based amateur cricketer named Ben Mummery, who had been tipped off about the series of events, was therefore able to post footage to X, where he dubbed it 'about the worst case of cheating I have ever seen in cricket'. By last night, that clip had clocked up more than six million views. Viewers then began to trawl the archives for other similar incidents. They promptly turned up dozens, suggesting that Saltburn (which, ironically, calls itself a 'friendly, sociable and inclusive cricket club') had been employing the cynical scam for more than a season. In almost every one of the clips that have emerged, the same portly man can be seen standing at first slip, clicking his fingers as the ball whistles past. He has been widely identified as Saltburn's opening batsman, one Brian Devine. One particularly damning video was posted by Rory Cotterill, the captain of Middlesbrough CC's second XI. He said there had been two more incidents like it in a single game they played on Saturday, June 27, which Saltburn won by 29 runs, 'leading to a 15 and 16-year-old being cheated out of an innings'. He added: 'I was at the non-striker's end at the time, unknowingly watching them cheat in real time'. Other cricket fans to weigh in included Piers Morgan, who dubbed the club's behaviour 'outrageous cheating' and a 'shameful scam'. Several posters dubbed Devine 'Clicky Ponting' – a play on the name of former Australian captain Ricky Ponting – on social media. Outrageous cheating, and just the tip of the iceberg from all that’s come out since it was exposed. Clicky Ponting (as he is now known) and various teammates at Saltburn CC, have clearly been at this shameful scam for years. Imagine doing this in local amateur cricket? Pathetic. https://t.co/fFOusuys4u — Piers Morgan (@piersmorgan) July 28, 2026 A formal investigation by the cricketing authorities is now under way. A statement from the North Yorkshire and South Durham League reads: 'The League has received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday 25 July 2026. A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete, no further comment will be made.' Disciplinary options include booting Saltburn out of the league, which has been running since 1892 and is one of 30-odd 'premier leagues' at the top level of recreational cricket in England and Wales. Sanctions could also involve giving individual players, or even the entire team, lifetime bans or suspensions from the game. For Devine, justice is perhaps already being served. The bespectacled businessman, who has played 481 matches in a 24-year amateur cricket career and was previously described on Saltburn's social media feeds as a 'legend' of the game, was last night reported to have been suspended by the club. I had earlier caught up with him by phone at Northallerton Auctions, a local livestock auction house where he works as company secretary. As cows mooed in the background, I asked whether he had any alternative explanation (aside from cheating) for the finger clicking. 'Naturally, I cannot comment on that,' he replied. 'I also cannot answer any questions because I am currently at work.' Devine, a bespectacled businessman who was previously described on Saltburn's social media feeds as a 'legend' of the game, was last night reported to have been suspended by the club Saltburn-by-the-Sea's historic cricket ground, with its white picket fence and neatly mown outfield, stood empty yesterday. Its team now face potentially being booted out the league Join the discussion How should cheating at even the lowest levels of sport be punished to protect fair play for all? Later, Devine faced the ignominy of being ditched by his official sponsor, a local Indian restaurant named Spices which he patronises regularly. Proprietor Akmol Hussain told the Daily Mail: 'I'm very shocked and disgusted by this video and can't believe that Brian would do something like this. I've met him many times, but he has damaged the reputation of cricket and my restaurant.' It was left to Georgina Vaughn, the mother of Devine's partner Clare, to defend his honour. 'It was only a little village cricket match and now it's become this thing that's all over the news and social media,' she said. 'It has got totally out of hand and there is nothing any of us want to say.' Asked whether Devine was a man of integrity, she replied: 'He certainly is.' Statistics suggest otherwise, however. They reveal that in the 13 matches that Devine has played for Saltburn this season, wicketkeepers have taken an astonishing 39 catches. In the seven that he hasn't played, they have managed just five. And in one single match, against Shildon Railway on July 18, no fewer than eight catches were claimed by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes. To put that number in perspective, the record for wicketkeeper catches taken in a single men's Test innings, over a period spanning 2,600 matches and 150 years, is a mere seven. Bowes, a local electrician, has been the main beneficiary of Clicky Ponting's scam. Despite only playing in about half the side's matches, he has taken 31 catches this season, which is ten more than any other keeper in the league. Last season, he only managed to take 12 catches, and the year before he had a mere six to his name. Wicketkeeper Josh Bowes, a local electrician, has been the main beneficiary of the scam. He has taken 31 catches this season, which is ten more than any other keeper in the league The haul equates to almost four catches for every single match in which Bowes has played. In matches where Bowes doesn't play, Saltburn's wicketkeepers have claimed a more normal haul of around one catch per game. Among the questions the league will now have to unpick is that of who, aside from Devine, was in on the scam. Videos of suspect wickets show several bowlers and fielders appealing with huge enthusiasm when the fielder clicks his fingers. Yet it is of course possible that they, like the umpire, believed they had heard the sound of bat on ball.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Your browser does not support iframes.

The truth about who knew what is likely to be found in the WhatsApp group in which team members discuss club affairs, though it's unclear whether investigators will have the power to compel the club to release it. At the bowls club next door to Saltburn's cricket club, a member suggested it was highly unlikely the organisation would go out of its way to co-operate, telling me: 'If the cheating has come from the top it would not surprise me. There are some nasty pieces of work among those who run it.' Whatever the outcome, the cheating scandal is just the latest in a long and ignoble tradition that stretches back to the earliest days of the sport, which generally results in rules being updated. In 1771, for example, Thomas White walked in to bat in a cricket match in Surrey, with a bat 'fully as wide as the wicket itself' making it impossible for him to be bowled out. Two days later, laws were passed limiting the maximum size to 4¼ inches. The 'Bodyline' Ashes series of 1932, in which England's bowlers aimed at the body and head of Australian batsmen in an attempt to nullify their star player Donald Bradman, led to rules changing to prevent large numbers of fielders being placed behind square on the leg side. And Trevor Chappell's famous decision to roll the ball on the ground in 1981 to prevent New Zealand achieving victory by hitting the last ball of a match for six, saw authorities update laws to make such deliveries illegal. Fast forward to 2018, and Australia's captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner were caught using sandpaper to rough up one side of the ball to help it move erratically in the air during a Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. And now, we might have to add Saltburn's very own opportunist to the scroll of dishonour of cheating cricketers: Clicky Ponting.

Sports.title: Latest on Manor Solomon's future amid West Ham interest - as Tottenham close in on deal for highly-rated Wolves youngster: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Bees hoping to seal Sangare deal

Lens are looking at Lorient's Arthur Avom Ebong and Melayro Bogarde from LASK as potential replacements for Brentford target Mamadou Sangare.

Brentford are discussing a £40million deal for Sangare, as reported by Daily Mail Sport, and hope to finalise terms quickly ahead of competition from the likes of Crystal Palace for the 24-year-old, who was named in the Ligue 1 Team of the Year last season.

Brentford are long-term admirers of the player and signing a new central midfielder was a priority even before Chelsea moved for Jordan Henderson. They also like Spurs' Pape Matar Sarr.

City teen heads to Leicester

Manchester City left back Christian McFarlane has joined Leicester on loan.

McFarlane, 19, becomes the third signing through the door at the King Power Stadium this summer. He joins Conor Chaplin and Alex McCarthy in bolstering Russell Martin's squad.

New Leicester boss Russell Martin has bolstered his team's promotion bid with the signing of Man City left back Christian McFarlane

McFarlane said: 'As a player, I’m intense and aggressive at both ends – attacking and defending. I like to make runs in behind and can be a bit of a nuisance for the opposition.

'The way [the manager] wants to play suits me perfectly, so I’m excited to get started.'

Blues close to landing Lund

Birmingham are closing on a deal for Palermo left back Kristoffer Lund.

The 24-year-old Dane spent last season on loan at Cologne but the German side did not take up their £2.5m option to buy.

Solomon set on permanent switch

Manor Solomon wants to leave Tottenham on a permanent transfer amid interest from West Ham.

The Israeli winger’s agent has made it clear he does not wish for another loan move, after spells with Leeds, Villarreal and Fiorentina, and that’s expected to suit Spurs as they look to recoup funds and upgrade their wide options.

Meanwhile, Spurs are closing on agreement with Wolves for Kwasi Senyah. The 16-year-old defensive midfielder and England youth international was wanted by several clubs but will join Spurs once terms are agreed and it is cleared by the FA.

Benfica are showing interest in Spurs left wing-back Souza while Leicester remain hopeful of taking 18-year-old centre back prospect Malachi Hardy.

Manor Solomon's Tottenham career has struggled to take-off since his move from Shakhtar Donetsk

Rovers return for Vaulks

Wales international Will Vaulks is in talks over a move to Tranmere.

The 32-year-old started his career with the Wirral club but never made a senior appearance.

Vaulks has gone on to play nearly 600 games at Sheffield Wednesday, Cardiff and Rotherham before arriving at Oxford United. He made 38 appearances in the Championship for them last season but is now looking to return home.

Tranmere have also snapped up goalkeeper Harrison Male on a one-year contract. The 25-year-old was a free transfer after he was released by York City earlier this summer.

He played 46 games as the Minstermen pipped Rochdale to the National League title and won Golden Glove after keeping 19 clean sheets.

Sports.title: Football must rally against Gianni Infantino's brazen bid to put World Cup up for sale - this is the most blatant ambush to disfigure sport imaginable, writes JONATHAN McEVOY
Sports.content:
Football must rally against Gianni Infantino's brazen bid to put World Cup up for sale - this is the most blatant ambush to disfigure sport imaginable, writes JONATHAN McEVOY

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It can now never be contradicted that Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump share a bone-deep appreciation of all that it means to best serve the world’s oldest and most popular game. Namely, the pursuit of money.

This endeavour has proved itself an enduringly compelling sport since the apple fell in the Garden, so it is as old as sin itself, and a pastime that today endangers bastardising modern football more deeply than any of the bank-lining panjandrums who went before them could ever have envisaged.

My goodness, others have tried hard to pollute sport. Juan Antonio Samaranch, the old Spanish fascist who sold the International Olympic Committee’s flaunted reputation for sporting purity all those years ago, gave it a good heave.

His self-acclaimed Excellency was reputed not to have earned a salary for his services in the name of progressing a vision set by the modern Olympics’ founding father Pierre de Coubertin. But in fawned-to, limousine-conveying grandeur he sold out his inheritance to dubious courtiers who militated against an ethic centred on guaranteeing a fair playing field for the youth of the world.

The youth of the world! Ha, if you will. The Olympic hymn, white doves at opening ceremonies, the oath sworn by an athlete on behalf of his fellow competitors in the name of honest competition. It was a pledge best uttered by the well-meaning, co-opted liar with crossed fingers behind his or her back.

We are, alas, inured to such hokum, a reality that reached its public apogee of infamy when Ben Johnson ran like a god in Seoul and was exposed as not quite the clock-defying deity we had hoped him to be.

Football needs to rebel against Gianni Infantino's (left) bid to sell the World Cup

Lance Armstrong, East Germany’s state-sponsored doping, the Fuentes drugs scandal in Spain, and so the list goes on. Indeed, WG Grace, cricket’s founding father, was no stranger to sharp practices in the Victorian Age. Old as sin itself, as we were saying, long before Allen Stanford, the Texan fraudster, promised huge, ill-begotten riches to cricket or LIV golf’s accumulators entered the stage with their distorting avarice bankrolled by Middle Eastern riyals.

Sport being traduced from within is endemic. Yet, we must still rail against this latest and unprecedented news, a departure in its arching scope, of Infantino effectively putting the World Cup itself up for sale to the highest bidder.

This when his chief elected responsibility as the head of FIFA, football’s world governing body and its supposed guarantor, is to preserve the verities of the game from malign speculators.

It is the most blatant and brazen ambush to disfigure sport in elected office imaginable.

To get back to Trump, and his recent phone call to Monaco-domiciled Infantino that represented the nadir of a largely successful World Cup. It all becomes clear, now.

We are speaking about the word Trump dripped into Infantino’s ear in his successful intervention to overturn US striker Folarin Balogun’s automatic one-match suspension. Political neutrality, a sine qua non of FIFA, was waved aside.

Infantino ludicrously claimed: ‘Potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide. It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.’

Trump scoffed at criticism of his meddling. ‘I understand sports well,’ the president bloviated, while admitting from the Oval Office that he did not know what a red card or its implications for a non-negotiable ban implied.

It is the most blatant and brazen ambush to disfigure sport in elected office imaginable

Infantino doubled down this week, opining: ‘To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 per cent safety and security, only joy and happiness.’

Thanks, Gianni. The dots can be joined now. Who is lined up to be a major investor in the scheme to sell shares in the World Cup to private investors? None other than Joshua Kushner, brother of Trump’s in-law Jared, a key agitator in taking the World Cup to America.

Trump and Infantino, who gave the former the bogus bauble of a peace prize, never awarded before and likely never to be awarded again, are in cahoots, hence the smoke they blow up each other’s posterior. US bank JPMorgan is also cited as a willing owner.

Under Infantino’s scheme, a company would be established to control the men’s and women’s World Cups and the Club World Cup. Which brings us to the point about money and what Infantino would be set to earn as a result of his brainchild.

All bosses of sporting bodies think a lot about this, their personal riches. They do not earn as much as the star performers, mostly men, accrue in the sport they (the governors) ‘serve’.

This disparity rankles. They want to get as rich as they can and seek to devise ways to do so.

So Infantino would, as it is understood, take on the role of ‘commissioner’ of his new World Cup order once his stint as FIFA president expires in 2031, offering him the potential to earn £37.5million a year, a some tenfold increase on his current wages. He will no doubt talk of wanting to grow the game. This is part of the playbook you would expect. He butters up the 211 members/sycophants who buttress his position – he will stand unopposed in office – by offering these supplicants shares in his folly, worth £15million to sell as they wish. That is nice earning possibilities for backwater associations if they then sublet their stakes.

And then we have the grotesque spectre of World Cups being staged more regularly than every four years, a dilution of world sport’s premier event, as all the moolah-grabbers look to exploit television rights deals, sponsorship, (exorbitant) ticket prices and hospitality sales on a more regular basis.

Joshua Kushner (pictured), brother of Trump’s in-law Jared, is lined up to be a major investor

The old framework of four-yearly World Cups would be swept away, just as wantonly as ‘hydration breaks’ were introduced spuriously over the last few weeks, with their advertising allure to TV networks clear.

Four quarters, rather than two halves, was a notion mooted, by the way, by Sepp Blatter ahead of the previous World Cup in America in 1994.

This latest abhorrence is of a different order. This, as Joseph Conrad wrote of another unchecked empire, is ‘a flabby, pretending, weak-eyed devil of a rapacious and pitiless folly’.

The emphasis is on greed, and football should rise up against it.

Sports.title: Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made
Sports.content:
Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made

Liverpool are targeting PSG winger Bradley Barcola this summer, and their chances of a deal have been boosted by former Reds forward Luis Diaz

View 2 Images Former Liverpool forward Luis Diaz has made a decision over his future (Image: David Ramos, Getty Images)

Bayern Munich winger Luis Diaz may have provided a boost to Liverpool's hopes of signing Bradley Barcola this summer. The Reds have been heavily linked with the PSG forward as they continue their search for a Mohamed Salah replacement.

‌



Salah left Anfield at the end of the season, leaving Liverpool searching for a way to replace his goals and assists. Barcola seems to be the player who has come out as the number one target, although a deal is expected to cost over £100 million.

‌



Our sister title The Liverpool ECHO reports that it is unlikely to put Andoni Iraola's side off making a move. They do, however, face competition from both Bayern Munich and Arsenal, and this is where Diaz comes in.

‌



Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp given strict instruction about managing Germany days after making quit threat READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Colombian has been a resounding success at the Allianz Arena since completing a £66million switch from Liverpool last summer. During his debut season in Germany, he netted 26 goals and laid on 23 assists across 51 appearances in all competitions.

That impressive form has attracted attention from Saudi outfit Al-Hilal. French publication L'Equipe claimed that the club were preparing to table an opening bid of at least €70million (£60m) for the wide man.

‌



However, Sky Germany reports that Diaz has informed Bayern that he wishes to remain at the club. The German champions are therefore unwilling to enter into negotiations with any club regarding a potential transfer, and have not placed an asking price on Diaz.

The 29-year-old still has three years left to run on his contract at the club. With Diaz's future appearing to be settled, this should bring Bayern's pursuit of Barcola to a close. With all of their attacking options remaining in place, they are unlikely to venture into the transfer market to bolster that area of their squad.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is emerging as a key transfer target for Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal are also said to be prioritising a move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior over Barcola. This could potentially leave Liverpool with a clear path to the PSG star.

The French club may have been more receptive to a transfer amid their pursuit of RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, who had also attracted Liverpool's attention. They have, however, been pipped to the post by Real Madrid.

PSG have since taken the remarkable step of issuing a statement confirming they have withdrawn from the race for the Ivory Coast international. "PSG has this evening officially withdrawn its interest and its bids for Yan Diomande," the statement read.

‌



"The asking transfer fee and salary demands were completely disproportionate and distortive - and PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance.

"As a two-time consecutive Champions League winner and the most successful club in recent years, PSG will also not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents - and will instead calmly and confidently continue its transfer planning."

Sports.title: Ranking Man Utd's four transfer priorities as exit set to change Michael Carrick's plans
Sports.content:
Four signings down, four to go? Manchester United have spent £85million this summer, bringing in two centre midfielders - Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans - and two goalkeepers - Karl Darlow and Kit Margetson.

And while United still want to strengthen one of those positions, they have other priorities. Michael Carrick was able to stick with a tight squad last season, often going more than seven days without a fixture thanks to the Red Devils being out of the both domestic cups by the time he took over.

But this season, United's return to the Champions League calls for more depth. That's why club chiefs want to bolster Carrick's options all over the pitch.

Midfield has long been the top priority, but with Santos and Tielemans through the door, and striker Joshua Zirkzee in talks to join Juventus on loan with a £30million option to buy, things have changed.

‌



With that in mind, Mirror Football is here to rank United's four transfer priorities.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd eye TWO strikers with Joshua Zirkzee closing in on transfer exit READ MORE :

Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery READ MORE :

Striker

Although Joshua Zirkzee only started one game under Carrick - after United had secured Champions League football - there's no doubt that his departure would leave a hole in the squad. The Dutchman played second fiddle to Benjamin Sesko last term and was needed in the final knockings of the campaign after Sesko picked up an injury which has also ruled him out of pre-season so far.

Zirkzee has started both of United's friendlies, scoring one goal and providing one assist, and is expected to lead the line again on Saturday against Atletico Madrid - unless he's in Italy sealing a move. Juventus are the frontrunners to sign him, with Roma and Como also interested.

‌



His impending exit should prompt United into the market for a replacement. Aston Villa's Ollie Watkins was of interest last summer while ex-Juventus striker Dusan Vlahovic is available on a free transfer.

Or should the Red Devils look outside the box? Ivan Toney scored 55 goals in Saudi Arabia last season and is proven in the Premier League, and prior to Chelsea's swoop, Danny Welbeck would've been an option.

Which position should Manchester United prioritise? Have your say in the comments section.

View 4 Images Manchester United would need a replacement for Joshua Zirkzee (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

‌



Centre midfield

Bumped down to second place from our last set of rankings, United have since addressed their previous top priority. It became even more important to sign at least two midfielders when, after Casemiro had left on a free transfer, Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious knee injury at the World Cup, ruling him out of much of the new season.

But given that Santos, Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo are the only fit senior centre midfielders in Carrick's squad, another wouldn't go a miss. Aurelien Tchouameni is understood to be United's No.1 target and the ex-Monaco star could be allowed to leave Real Madrid if they sign Rodri from Manchester City.

Roma's Manu Kone has also been shortlisted alongside Bournemouth youngster Alex Scott. However, United are unlikely to make a bid for Scott, with Chelsea having seen a £64m offer rejected by Chelsea.

View 4 Images Aurelien Tchouameni is a target for Manchester United (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Left-back

To the defence now and despite Luke Shaw managing to start all 38 Premier League games last season for the first time in his career, his fitness will always remain a concern. Shaw, 31, remains susceptible to injury and playing every few days would likely be too much.

Patrick Dorgu has developed into more of a left winger and with United open to selling Harry Amass, it's clear that they'd like to bring in a new left-back. Newcastle's Lewis Hall is understood to be on their radar and reportedly open to a move to Old Trafford.

But given that Newcastle have already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali - and are in advanced talks with Arsenal over Bruno Guimaraes - it may well be impossible to sign Hall for a reasonable price. Fulham defender Antonee Robinson is an alternative.

View 4 Images Lewis Hall is keen to join Manchester United, according to reports (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



Left wing

If Barcelona had triggered their option to sign Marcus Rashford for just £26m, signing a left winger would've been higher on United's to-do list. But with Rashford back in the fold, it makes things complicated.

There seems to be no active escape route for the England international right now and he's set to return to training in the coming weeks to work under Carrick for the second time. But things can change, and United are open to selling Rashford for around £40m.

Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye is admired by the Red Devils and said to be open to a transfer amid interest from Al-Hilal. Lille's Matias Fernandez-Pardo has also been touted, a lesser-known name who would be a cheaper option to serve as backup to Matheus Cunha.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta could be forced to break his own Arsenal rule in major transfer U-turn
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta could be forced to break his own Arsenal rule in major transfer U-turn

Arsenal are exploring several blockbuster transfers after winning the Premier League title

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta looks to have changed his policy (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

Mikel Arteta may to have ditch his own rule if Arsenal are to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid. The Gunners are interested in making an audacious move for the Brazil superstar, who remains in contract talks with Los Blancos with just a year remaining on his current deal.

‌



The Gunners would have to cough up a British record £137m to sign the 26-year-old, according to reports in Spain. Vinicius would also command wages of at least £400,000, making him the club's best-paid player.

‌



That would represent an about-turn from Arteta, who axed players on similar wages after taking charge in 2019. The likes of Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, who were on at least £350,000 per week, were moved on early in the Spaniard's reign.

‌



Arsenal have recently revisited those kinds of sums by awarding Bukayo Saka a new contract worth £365,000 a week. However, as a homegrown talent and loyal servant to the club, he arguably deserves such rewards.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Handing a new signing such a gargantuan deal would see the club revisit the vast salaries that were occasionally dished out during the final years of Arsene Wenger's reign.

‌



Arsenal news: Vinicius Jr in Real Madrid standoff as price tag problem laid bare READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr has already promised to join club as Arsenal handed transfer timeline READ MORE :

With a first Premier League crown in more than two decades in the bag and the club on such a strong financial footing, such wages are within the club's range. They could also become commonplace as Areta looks to keep the key members of his title-winning squad together.

As for Vinicius, his future at Real is uncertain following Jose Mourinho's return. The Portuguese, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabeu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinicius accused Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February.

View 3 Images Arteta is looking to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty )

‌



Mourinho, Benfica manager at the time, said "something happens, always" in matches where Vinicius plays. Prestianni was banned for six matches after he admitted to using homophobic language towards Vinicius.

However, Mourinho has reportedly made it clear he wants big players like Vinicius to remain at the club. Talks between the player's representatives and Real are continuing and there is said to be a will on both sides for a new contract to be agreed.

View 3 Images Mesut Ozil commanded a huge salary at Arsenal (Image: GLYN KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



But if it isn't, they are likely to cash in this summer to avoid losing him for nothing in a year's time. Arsenal, who have also been linked with Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez and Bradley Barcola of PSG, have bolstered their attacking options with the £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.

But bringing in a player of Vinicius' calibre and profile would take their summer business to a completely different level and send a clear message to their Premier League rivals.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposal could trigger £51m Man Utd transfer
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford swap deal proposal could trigger £51m Man Utd transfer

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford is set to return to the club, with his future uncertain, but Old Trafford chiefs may have the opportunity to offload the academy product

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could be used in a swap deal (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester United could use Marcus Rashford in a bid to land Roma star Manu Kone. The Red Devils are looking to continue their midfield reinforcement push, and the Frenchman has been the subject of their interest.

‌



United have so far been unwilling to meet Roma's £51million asking price, but Gazzetta dello Sport in Italy suggest that Rashford could provide a suitable makeweight to get a deal over the line. Kone is poised to leave the Stadio Olimpico this summer as the Italian look to fund their own transfer plans and adhere to Financial Fair Play regulations.

‌



Roma have fielded multiple enquiries regarding the Frenchman, but neither United nor Al Ahli have been convinced by that valuation. Reports claim that Michael Carrick's side could take advantage of Roma's desire to sign a left-sided forward.

‌



However, the England international's wages would present difficulties for the Italians. They would require United to foot up a significant portion of Rashford's salary for a loan arrangement.

United chiefs prefer a permanent exit for Rashford after his loan spells to Barcelona and Aston Villa both ended without a move being made permanent. A successful stint at Camp Nou did not even get a deal over the line.

Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe READ MORE :

The Catalan outfit declined to sign Rashford permanently despite possessing an option to acquire the 28-year-old for £26m. They opted instead to recruit Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United.

‌



No club has yet met United's asking price for Rashford, while reports suggest the academy graduate turned down the prospect of a move to Turkey. As it stands, Rashford looks set to return to Old Trafford.

The forward has not featured for the club since December 2024, but still has two years left to run on his contract. A clause that would have permitted him to leave for £40m - to any club other than Liverpool or Manchester City - has now expired.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is set to return to Manchester United for the moment (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Rashford remains United's highest earner, pocketing £325,000 per week and accounting for a considerable chunk of the club's wage bill. While the board will be eager to shed that financial burden, Michael Carrick indicated at the end of last season that he was open to the idea of the forward staying put.

"Whoever's here, I want to work with, and help them improve," Carrick said. "At the moment, it's this squad of players. There's obviously players on loan, and whatever happens with that later on will happen.

Article continues below

"But certainly, as a coach, and leader of a squad, we want to get the best out of everyone."

Sports.title: Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks
Sports.content:
Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) have been approached by a consortium led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia over buying a minority stake in the club

View 2 Images Jeff Bezos has been approached over investing in Liverpool (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group remain in talks with a consortium interested in buying a minority stake in Liverpool, the club's chief executive Billy Hogan has confirmed.

‌



FSG released a statement last week saying that Amit Bhatia had expressed an interest in buying a stake in Liverpool. The British-Indian businessman was the director and co-owner at QPR for 18 seasons and has the backing of the the Mittal family, who are worth £26bn, according to Forbes.

‌



Despite being the son-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal, who leads ArcelorMittal, the globe's biggest steel and mining firm, Bhatia has reportedly approached Jeff Bezos about joining his consortium. The Amazon founder, the fourth-richest man in the world with a net worth of over £190bn, is said to be considering the prospect.

‌



Asked for an update on the situation, Hogan told Bloomberg: "I can only refer back to the statement from FSG last week that we have been approached by a consortium that's led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia for a strategic minority investment in the club. And I wouldn't say anything than that at this point."

Liverpool star confirms Mo Salah contact as true impact of star's exit made clear READ MORE :

FSG bought Liverpool in 2010 when they were on the verge of administration for £300m and, according to the Financial Times, the potential deal being outlined by Bhatia would value the club at £4.5bn. They previously sold a single-figure stake to global sports investment firm Dynasty Equity in 2023 and are now weighing up another deal.

This deal is understood to only be at the preliminary stages, but is for a much more significant stake, potentially 30 per cent of the club.

‌



Bezos has previously been credited with an interest in buying NFL franchises, with the Washington Commanders and Seattle Seahawks on his radar. Neither has materialised thus far and the Amazon billionaire's investment would be much smaller if he did become involved with Liverpool.

View 2 Images Amit Bhatia is leading the consortium (Image: Andrew Fosker/REX/Shutterstock)

Liverpool have won the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup and Carabao Cup since FSG's arrival 16 years ago, but are entering a period of flux. Andoni Iraola has arrived to replace Arne Slot following a disappointing 2025/26 season, while Michael Edwards left his role as FSG's chief executive of football earlier this month.

Article continues below

Edwards joined Liverpool in 2011 and was promoted to sporting director in 2016 before leaving in the summer of 2022. His departure is a significant blow to FSG and Liverpool while there has also been speculation over the future of Liverpool sporting director Richard Hughes.

Sports.title: Arsenal told Real Madrid have 'obligation to sell' Vinicius Jr as Spanish media back transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal told Real Madrid have 'obligation to sell' Vinicius Jr as Spanish media back transfer

Arsenal have been linked with Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior and media in Spain have backed the blockbuster transfer

View 3 Images Vinicius Junior has been linked with a colossal transfer to Arsenal (Image: Getty)

Spanish media believe Vinicius Junior could still join Arsenal this transfer window. This is despite widespread reports suggesting the Real Madrid and Brazil star will stay put.

‌



The Gunners head into the new season as defending Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years and have looked to sharpen their attack. Christos Tzolis has already been signed from Belgian side Club Brugge for £34million, but Mikel Arteta seemingly wants more.

‌



Last week, news surfaced that Arsenal were exploring a move to sign Vinicius Junior, which would likely be the window's headline transfer. However, more recent updates suggest he is keen to remain at the Bernabeu and pen fresh terms, with his current deal set to expire in 2027.

‌



Irrespective of the suggestion that Vinicius won't be going anywhere, some outlets in Spain reckon that his club have an "obligation" to sell him and that there could be more to this narrative than meets the eye.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal can offer Vinicius Jr key non-negotiable that Real Madrid cannot after transfer update READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr has already promised to join club as Arsenal handed transfer timeline READ MORE :

Ex-Real Madrid goalkeeper Santi Canizares spoke on COPE's Tiempo de Juego programme about the Vinicius saga and thinks that his former side would rather sell their star than see him leave for free next summer.

‌



View 3 Images Vinicius's current contract expires in 2027 (Image: Getty)

"The more noise there is about a player, the less chance he has of leaving," he stated. "[But] Real Madrid are late with everything. If it's true that he doesn't have a signed agreement, Real Madrid have an obligation to sell him. You can't lose 100 or 100-plus million euros by letting a player's contract expire. I just don't believe it's going to happen. It's an unforgivable mismanagement."

The fee many reports claim Vinicius would cost this summer is in the £100m-plus range. But with the likes of Sky Sports News reporting that he will stay and that Real Madrid have zero interest in selling him, it could be that a new deal is signed rather than a groundbreaking transfer sanctioned.

‌



However, one Spanish outlet hints that there hasn't been a meeting about renewing Vinicius's contract for some time and suggests there could be more to come regarding the 26-year-old's future. Deputy director of AS, Tomas Roncero, states: "The club says there probably won't be a problem, because he intends to renew.

"If you talk to Vini's people, they tell you that his only wish is to stay at Madrid and leaving isn't even on his mind. But curiously, there hasn't been a single meeting for eight or nine months. The last time, there was a huge financial disagreement, because his demand was to earn the same as Kylian Mbappe. Madrid made it clear to him that he's not going to earn the same as Mbappe.

"There will be no agreement on those initial terms. I'd like to think that Vinicius will lower his financial demands, which would also be reasonable. You have to understand the pecking order within a club and it's clear that Real Madrid's star player is Mbappe.

‌



View 3 Images One Spanish outlet thinks wages could become an issue because of Kylian Mbappe (Image: Getty)

"He's the all-time leading goalscorer in World Cup history, World Cup Golden Boot winner, Champions League Golden Boot winner, and La Liga top scorer. His individual statistics speak for themselves. And Vini hasn't been quite as outstanding. He has to understand that he can't earn the same amount."

On Vinicius potentially leaving for free, he added: "Real Madrid want to avoid that scenario. The Yan Diomande deal is a clear message that Vinicius might not stay. Otherwise, there wouldn't be such urgency to spend 120 million euros on a 19-year-old player. Such a big gamble only makes sense if you're also covering your back."

Article continues below

Roncero's colleague and chief editor of AS, Aritz Gabilondo, also stated: "If both sides want to renew, the deal is signed and that's it. Someone here is playing a different game.

"It’s a strategy that Real Madrid – and specifically its president – has historically taken a dim view of. Taking a gamble on Florentino Pérez in this instance is very tricky."

Sports.title: FA 'deeply concerned' as they issue statement on FIFA's plan to sell off World Cup
Sports.content:
FA 'deeply concerned' as they issue statement on FIFA's plan to sell off World Cup

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is under fire amid plans to sell shares in the World Cup, sparking anger from fans and confederations such as UEFA, who have accused him of 'crossing a line'

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino wants private investors in the World Cup (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

The Football Association have released a statement saying that it is 'deeply concerned' by Gianni Infantino's plans to sell off the World Cup. FIFA announced on Tuesday - after reports leaked its plans - that it intended to expand 'football development funding' to more than $10billion (£7.5bn) by inviting third-party investment to its competitions, including the World Cup.

‌



It has been claimed that Infantino could make millions from private investors. European confederation UEFA issued a strongly-worded statement accusing FIFA of 'crossing the line', while the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that FIFA had 'sold out'.

‌



Now the FA have spoken out in a statement published on Wednesday which read: "We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

‌



"Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved. When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gary Lineker shows FIFA disgust in four-word response to Gianni Infantino bombshell READ MORE :

UEFA nations could BOYCOTT World Cup in light of FIFA's plot to sell tournament READ MORE :

Alongside UEFA, CONCACAF - the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football - have joined the criticism. "CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release," it began.

‌



"We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process. We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

"As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, Fifa, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

"This is the framework within which CONCACAF operates. We trust that all within the Fifa family will act in the same manner."

‌



Should the confederations break away from FIFA? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images UEFA attacked FIFA in a strongly-worded statement (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

UEFA will hold emergency talks on Wednesday and could discuss breaking away from FIFA competitions in what would be a drastic move. "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," the European body said.

‌



"UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

Sports.content:
Man Utd open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick wields transfer axe

Michael Carrick is continuing his Manchester United rebuild ahead of a return to the Champions League

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has reportedly made four more important Man United transfer decisions. (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United are reportedly open to offers for four more players as Michael Carrick continues his Old Trafford rebuild ahead of a return to the Champions League. The Reds will listen to offers for Harry Amass, Dan Gore, Toby Collyer and Radek Vitek.

‌



There have already been enquiries made for goalkeeper Vitek - who impressed on loan with Bristol City in the Championship last season - and young left-back Harry Amass. It's claimed that both loan and permanent deals are being explored.

‌



Gore and Collyer also spent last season on loan away from the club and they could follow a similar path this summer. Until then, the quartet will continue to train with Carrick's squad until the first-team stars who were in World Cup action, return to the squad.

‌



Man Utd eye TWO strikers with Joshua Zirkzee closing in on transfer exit READ MORE :

Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery READ MORE :

The four want regular action next season and as things stand, their most likely route will be through Under-21s football and United want a more compeitive environment, according to the Daily Mail.

The Athletic claim that Amass, who impressed against Rosenborg last weekend, could be available for a £6m fee.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Amass could leave Man United this summer (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

The four stars join the list of players who could leave Old Trafford this summer, with Joshua Zirkzee and Marcus Rashford also likely to depart.

Zirkzee has attracted the attention of several clubs in Italy, where he impressed for Bologna prior to joining United.

‌



The Dutch international has struggled for consistency since his move to the Premier League and now Juventus are reportedly in talks to sign the 25-year-old. Other reports claim Como, AS Roma and AC Milan are keen on signing Zirkzee, with United open to offers.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
