World.title: New Narva mayor: There really are many problems that need immediate action
World.content:
Newly elected Narva Mayor Jaan Toots said the 21‑kilometer heating pipeline being built between the city and the Auvere power plant will cut heating prices for Narva residents by nearly half. He said the biggest problem is unemployment.

Last Sunday the Narva City Council passed a no‑confidence motion against Mayor Katri Raik and chose Toots as her replacement.

Did the transfer of power go smoothly?

It could be watched live. Naturally the new council chair, who led a meeting for the first time, was upset. There were some hiccups in how the meeting was conducted, but all of that is forgivable because people's nerves were stretched to the limit. Today it is already history.

The new coalition's majority is extremely narrow. How do you plan to make sure none of the 16 council members currently on your side are lured away? How likely is that?

A group of 16 managed to stay together in the opposition for four and a half months in a situation where three or four members were enticed every day with all kinds of offers. They stayed together on principle, believing a different working style was needed. I think that now, when we hold power ourselves, I see no reason why anyone would leave. There is a lot of unfinished work, and we will move forward from here.

You will certainly need very strong and loyal deputy mayors. Can you already say who they might be?

We agreed to announce the names after the city government is confirmed on Saturday. At 10 a.m. Saturday there will be a short council meeting to confirm the government, and on Monday I will set the work order and assign responsibilities. I can say this much: there will be two deputy mayors, maybe a third in the future. (The draft Narva council decision reveals that the new deputy mayors will be Oleg Karpikov and Eduard Parts -ed.)

Narva power struggle has been unprecedented in Estonia and has lasted a long time. Has your side actually offered anything to council members?

No, one council member simply came over to us, and that happened already in February. We look to the future, and I hope we now have a calm working environment. When I walk around Narva, many people wish us success and want that calm to continue.

Do you currently live in Narva?

I live in Narva, yes. On weekends I am at home in Tartu, but during the week I live in Narva. Weekends vary, and you know that a mayor's job is 24/7. If needed, you must be present. So yes, I live in Narva.

When you walk around Narva and look around, what do you see as the biggest problems that need to be solved?

Yesterday I had the chance to speak with the head of the European Union representation in Estonia, and we will meet on August 12 to bring new funding to Narva. Under Katri Raik no new projects were started; she finished the projects we began.

A few things have been delayed a bit, but construction of a new hotel in downtown Narva will definitely begin. I spoke with the owners yesterday, and it will have 132 rooms. Today Narva's four hotels together have only 152 rooms. Capacity will double, but it is still a drop in the ocean. It is very hard to bring people to Narva to enjoy the views and learn about history when we have nowhere to accommodate them.

Second, we are about to finish furnishing 12 social housing buildings that have already been constructed. They were built under Raik, and designed under us. Now they only need furniture. I think we will open them around October.

We have several major projects. A big concern is the music school, which is certainly the oldest on Estonian territory, built in the tsarist era. The school celebrated its 125th anniversary last year. Estonia is younger, and this school building needs a replacement. The current building is practically at risk of collapse.

There really are many problems that need immediate action.

From Tallinn's perspective, Narva residents' main problem seems to be high heating prices?

I say the main problem is unemployment. Our unemployment rate fluctuates between 12.8 and over 13 percent, while Estonia's average is around six to seven percent. Thirty‑one percent of our residents are pensioners, and most of those who work earn only minimum wage. The living environment is extremely harsh, and the biggest problem is jobs and unemployment.

Young people leave, even though we have opportunities to work in industry. We also have the opposite effect: many factories and companies use labor not only from Tartu and Tallinn but also from other European Union countries because of a shortage of specialists. We must start addressing this.

Of course high heating prices are also a problem, but that issue is now being resolved. When I first became mayor, in October 2023 I immediately proposed building a 21‑kilometer pipeline. Steam released from energy production can be pumped to the city and used for heating. The price depends on the cost of the pipeline, and heating prices will drop by nearly half. We must make sure the pipeline is ready for next year's heating season.

Another major problem is that electricity prices rose on July 1. This slows our production capacity — factories are starting to consider whether it is worth developing and expanding production in Narva at all because of high electricity prices. These are today's problems.

For many people in Estonia, running Narva seems surrounded by a kind of mystique. If we call you in half a year, will you still be Narva's mayor?

Unfortunately that is how it is, but if we look at the situation in Narva today, things are not better elsewhere — first Tallinn, and now again Pärnu. That is politics.

World.title: Estonia's women's épée team climb to number 4 in the world
World.content:
The Estonian women's épée team have risen three spots to fourth place in the international fencing rankings after their strong performance at the world championships which saw them take team silver.

This means also that the team is in strong contention for qualification to the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

The foursome of Julia Beljajeva, Irina Embrich, Katrina Lehis and Veronika Zuikova performed disappointingly in the individual events in Hong Kong, but came together as a team to go all the way to the finals, losing to Olympic champions Italy by just a point, 31-30.

Before the world championships, Estonia was ranked seventh. The performance reached 291 points overall which moved them up three spaces in the world rankings, especially as on the way to the final they overcame Olympic runners-up France in the quarter finals, and reigning European silver medalists Hungary in the semis.

Only South Korea in first place (376 points), Italy (316) and the U.S. (296) are ahead of Estonian in the table now.

The promotion is also significant as the top four teams in the rankings automatically qualify for the next Olympic Games in Los Angeles in two years' time. They will be joined by the top teams from each of the four worldwide zones.

The qualification period for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics begins on April 1 next year.

Three of the four who competed in Hong Kong – Lehis, Beljajeva and Embrich, were in the team which took team gold at the Tokyo Olympics held in 2021, while Lehis took individual bronze at the same games. In Paris two years ago, another fencer, Nelli Differt, was just outside the medals in the individual category.

The épée class uses a heavier thrusting weapon where the entire body is a valid target, whereas the lighter foil is a thrusting weapon restricted to the torso for points-scoring purposes.

World.title: Advertising agencies: AI overuse erodes a company's credibility
World.content:
AI is getting to be a powerful tool in advertising, but excessive or inappropriate use could harm companies, marketers and advertisers have warned.

AI overuse could lead to more misinformation appearing in the public sphere, as well as misleading customers and ultimately damage companies' credibility.

Media reports have recently pointed out the phenomenon of event posters and s which have seemingly been created using AI

Anniken Haldna, CEO of the Estonian Association of Marketing Communication Agencies, said nearly 80 percent of international firms already use AI in advertising, primarily to save time and money. However, Haldna added that AI is still mainly used as a tool. Human beings are still behind the overall creative drive of an ad, she said. "Human creativity, the human strategic perspective and dimension of marketing – that is critically important."

Alvar Lonks, creative director at Tallinn ad agency Tabasco, confirmed AI has made the work at his company faster and more efficient.

"From an agency's point of view, I can say that it makes things like creating mock-ups much easier. In the past, we had to do a lot of drawing, which took many working hours, but thanks to AI, producing mock-ups is much simpler," Lonks explained.

He agreed that AI still lacks creativity aspects, and it would not be viable to create high-quality, distinctive advertising from start to finish using AI alone. AI in ad production is nonetheless here to stay, Lonks added.

AI apps on a smartphone. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Above all, the use of AI should not be deceptive, he noted. "People generally like s that speak to them, that use their language or show them familiar images. Authenticity is what matters here," Lonks said.

Haldna added the biggest challenge going forward is helping companies stand out, given ads with significant AI input tend to look a bit uniform. She also highlighted the spread of misinformation, and the challenge of earning customers' trust while still using AI.

"Critical thinking about the use of AI in marketing is vital, including from the perspective of our association. We would certainly encourage people to think critically and also to consider the issue of trust. The initial global studies suggest that people actually do not trust AI-generated s," Haldna went on.

Haldna and Lonks concluded that even as AI is a useful tool for producing s, advertising will remain human-centred for the foreseeable future.

"Creative people are at the heart of an agency, not artificial intelligence. That human perspective is essential if we want to create valuable marketing communications that genuinely resonate with people," Haldna said.

"It is not a case of writing a single prompt, getting a result and immediately printing it on a huge billboard," Lonks noted.

World.title: New nature-focused spa hotel opens on Lake Peipus in Ida-Viru County
World.content:
A new spa has opened on the shores of Lake Peipus in eastern Estonia for the first time in more than 40 years, offering guests a break from the daily grind and the possibility to relax in nature.

Kurro Nature Spa Hotel is the first major holiday complex to be built on the northern shore of Lake Peipus in more than 40 years. The buildings, constructed in the forest, seem to have been lowered into place by helicopter.

Visitors are sold the opportunity of leaving daily life behind and relaxing in unspoilt nature.

Kurro Nature Spa's managing director, Killu Maidla, believes this is what people need as society becomes increasingly fast-paced and digitized.

"There simply isn't a place where you can go to the countryside, into the forest, into nature, listen to the wind rustling through the treetops and watch the wild, foaming August waves on Lake Peipus, while at the same time enjoying good service, a pleasant environment and a cosy room," said Kurro founder Andres Linnas.

He believes that the more time passes, the more society will need this type of holiday.

The spa will open the northern shore of Lake Peipus to year-round tourism and bring nearly 100 new jobs to Alutaguse Municipality.

Alutaguse Mayor Tauno Võhmar acknowledged that the first few years would certainly attract everyone who is curious and wants to visit the spa at least once. He added that long-term sustainability would be the biggest challenge.

There are already seven spas in Ida-Viru County. The arrival of the distinctive Kurro will increase competition, but will also bring more tourists.

Karina Küppas, managing director of Narva-Jõesuu Medical SPA, explained that Ida-Viru County will receive positive PR. That, in turn, will draw attention to the region. She added that demand may not currently be as great as the level of supply that is emerging.

The spa cost €37 million to build, one-third of which was funded by the Just Transition Fund.

World.title: Minister: Estonia sends extra border guards to Latvia as Belarus drives migrant surge
World.content:
Estonia will send additional police and border guard forces to Latvia to strengthen the European Union's external border. The decision came after several dozen illegal migrants who entered the country through Belarus and Latvia were detained in Estonia in recent days.

Pressure on the Latvian‑Belarusian section of the border is growing, and attempts to cross illegally have increased significantly in recent weeks.

Interior Minister Igor Taro, who visited the Latvian‑Belarusian border last week, said the situation there is very serious.

"It is rush hour at the border, you could say. The Belarusian regime is deliberately sending these migrants into the forest, gathering them in special camps, preparing them, giving them all kinds of tools to overcome obstacles on Latvia's external state border. The situation is quite complicated," he said.

"This is part of Russia's overall aggression tactics, and Belarus is their ally. Even if they are not acting actively in a military sense, they still support logistics and various relays used to direct drones toward Ukraine. And one form of this supportive activity is sending illegal migrants toward European countries that help Ukraine, to create additional problems and force them to spend resources," the minister continued.

He said illegal migrants create problems for the entire society. When migration centers are overcrowded, resources are needed to house these people and to find interpreters and other specialists. All this creates a serious burden that Latvia feels most acutely right now, but there have also been cases of people detained on Estonian territory.

In recent days, more than 30 migrants who entered Europe after illegally crossing the Belarusian border were detained in Tallinn.

Taro said Estonia is much better prepared today for possible migration challenges than it was several years ago. In recent years the state has steadily strengthened the external border: a border fence has been built, and work continues on installing modern surveillance systems and other equipment to control the area.

He also stressed that the fence itself is not an absolute barrier. Its main purpose is to give border guards time to respond to attempts to cross illegally.

At Belarus-Lithuania border, underground digging attempted

Lithuanian border guards discovered an underground tunnel near the Belarus border recently that may have been built to move illegal migrants into the country. The tunnel already extended several meters into Lithuanian territory, but an exit had not yet been completed.

Estonian Police and Border Guard Board deputy director for border management Veiko Kommusaar said in an interview that there is no information suggesting anyone has tried to dig such a tunnel on Estonia's eastern border, but it cannot be ruled out in the future. History shows attempts to bring contraband alcohol or other goods underwater using cables or even divers.

Stenbocki maja sisehoovis esitleti droonide teekaarti 2026–2030 Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Kommusaar added that Estonia's land border is well covered by various surveillance and camera systems. "Surveillance systems are definitely something that shows activity levels. These tunnels are not dug by hand."

Of Estonia's 130 kilometers of land border with Russia, 110 kilometers are essentially fenced, and more than half of the surveillance systems have been installed. The infrastructure will be completed in 2027, ensuring full surveillance coverage along the entire border.

In Belarus, tunnels are being dug because the pressure to enter the European Union illegally is so great that all possible methods are being tried. "This is actually enabled by the Belarusian regime itself. You cannot just dig something in a border area. Belarusian border guards facilitate this activity and provide information on possible crossing points at specific times," he added.

Kommusaar said migration pressure on Latvia and Lithuania comes from Belarus, while no similar migration attack is currently being carried out from Russian territory. At the moment there are no signs the Russian Federation is organizing anything similar, but that could change overnight.

Why is there no pressure from Russia now? "One could speculate that if Belarus is doing the dirty work for them, part of the answer lies there."

Kommusaar said this migration attack in our region has been ongoing for five years. Every day more than 100 people are blocked from entering the European Union at the Latvian border. Unfortunately not all attempts are stopped, and some still manage to cross.

This article has been updated on July 29 with comments by Estonian Police and Border Guard Board deputy director for border management Veiko Kommusaar.

World.title: State considers replacing bankruptcy trustees with civil servants
World.content:
Justice Minister Liisa Pakosta is proposing to replace bankruptcy trustees with civil servants or to cover trustee fees from the state budget in certain proceedings. The state's Insolvency Service said the idea is worthwhile, and one way to fund it could be an insolvency tax.

The Ministry of Justice said Estonia's insolvency system is not sustainable in its current form. As a result, problems must be addressed to prevent the entire system from collapsing.

A bankruptcy trustee is an impartial official appointed by a court whose main task is to manage and carry out bankruptcy proceedings. The trustee acts as an intermediary who must protect the legal interests of both the debtor and creditors and ensure transparency.

One way to make the insolvency system more sustainable, the ministry said, would be to cover trustee fees from the state budget in cases where there is no property or only minimal assets.

Right now trustees cannot declare bankruptcy if it is clear there is no property. "No one pays the trustee from the state budget or from creditors' pockets when there are no assets. If a deposit is paid, bankruptcy is declared, but if it is not paid, then it is not declared because there simply is no property," said Andres Hermet from Estonian Chamber of Enforcement Agents and Trustees in Bankruptcy

Bankruptcy proceedings (illustrative). Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

The ministry said trustees should not have to perform mandatory work for an unknown period without any guarantee of reasonable compensation. If the state paid reasonable compensation, the ministry said the quality of bankruptcy proceedings could improve.

The ministry did not specify how much the possible solution would cost the state. It noted that the budget impact could be significant.

Hermet said such additional state funding is a good idea, because no one would refuse money if the state wants to invest in the field.

But he did not agree with the ministry's assessment that the insolvency system is collapsing. He said new recruits are needed because entering the profession is difficult for people who have never been trustees, and trustee fees are completely unpredictable.

The Ministry of Justice said that if civil servants handled bankruptcy proceedings, it would mean additional costs for the state budget. Under this solution, civil servants would need salaries, and there would be IT development, space and support service costs, training costs and transition costs. The ministry said the state's workload would increase significantly.

Signe Viimsalu Autor/allikas: Kirke Ert/ERR

Insolvency Service head Signe Viimsalu said creating such a state competence center would be the most reasonable option.

Viimsalu wrote to Prime Minister Kristen Michal last week, saying that widespread insolvency could cause economic, social and institutional uncertainty and pose a threat to Estonia's internal security.

Viimsalu said the system that has been in place for the past 30 years urgently needs reform so creditors can recover their money more effectively. She said it would be an additional cost for the state budget, but in the long run it would be the most reasonable and cost‑effective solution for society as a whole.

She also could not say how much it would cost the state to nationalize the current trustee system. "I think the ministries need to calculate that themselves," Viimsalu said.

The Insolvency Service head said there are several ways to fund a new type of system.

"Certain proceedings could be handled entirely by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry's arbitration court. One option is to create an insolvency tax in Estonia to fund the system. Another option is a middle ground where, for example, wrongdoers pay part of the system's costs. Another option is that the bankruptcy estate itself funds part of the system, such as the IT system," Viimsalu said.

Viimsalu said the idea of an insolvency tax still needs more thought.

Hermet from the trustees' chamber said any proposal to create state bankruptcy trustees is not adequate.

"I do not see any economic logic in this. The issue where I have no criticism of the service is that we are fighting against bankruptcy masters and late bankruptcy filings. But a state trustee would not help solve this problem in any way."

He added that he does not see how a civil servant could work more effectively or cheaply than a bankruptcy trustee.

World.title: Iraqi leaders condemn attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Prominent Iraqi figures, notably Shiite cleric Muqtada al-Sadr, have openly criticized Iran-backed militias for seeking to pull Iraq into a larger regional conflict by launching unlawful drone attacks on neighboring Saudi Arabia.

In a statement on X, al-Sadr strongly criticized the militias for their dangerous actions, which jeopardize the security of the Iraqi people.

Al-Sadr’s remarks came after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes on Iran-backed groups in several Iraqi provinces on Wednesday.

Influential Iraqi political and religious figures are escalating the pressure to disarm militant groups across the country.

The US-Saudi airstrikes were an immediate response to many drone assaults carried out by militias in the past few days against US interests in the region as well as oil facilities in Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad has initiated investigations into cross-border drone assaults in an effort to strengthen national sovereignty and prevent illegitimate military actions.

Iraqi officials confirmed that the country will not be used to launch attacks against countries in the region.

World.title: US Embassy issues new security alert, urges Americans not to travel to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Embassy in Baghdad on Wednesday issued a security alert advising American citizens to avoid travel to Iraq, following a series of attacks that it said were carried out by Iran-aligned militias targeting locations inside Iraq and across the region.

In the alert, the embassy urged U.S. nationals currently in Iraq to remain vigilant, closely monitor local media, and follow instructions issued by Iraqi authorities.

The embassy also warned that air travel could be affected without prior notice, including possible flight delays, cancellations, or temporary airspace closures.

As a result, American citizens planning to travel were advised to check directly with their airlines before heading to airports, as flight schedules may change at any time.

The mission reiterated that Iraq remains under the U.S. State Department’s Level 4: Do Not Travel advisory, citing terrorism, kidnapping, armed conflict, civil unrest, and the U.S. government’s limited ability to provide emergency services to its citizens in the country.

In addition to avoiding unnecessary travel, the embassy encouraged U.S. citizens already in Iraq to maintain communication with family members, ensure travel documents remain valid, and keep mobile phones fully charged.

The advisory also urged Americans to avoid protests and demonstrations, maintain a low profile, stay aware of their surroundings, and enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive security updates.

Furthermore, the embassy advised citizens to follow official U.S. State Department security alerts and remain prepared for rapidly changing conditions.

The advisory comes amid heightened security tensions across Iraq and the wider region.

Earlier this week, Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani said the region had recently come under drone attacks launched from the direction of Nineveh, stressing the need for an effective air defense system to protect the Kurdistan Region.

Days earlier, coalition forces intercepted eight explosive-laden drones targeting Erbil. The Kurdistan Region’s Counter-Terrorism Service said all of the drones were successfully destroyed before reaching their targets, with no casualties reported.

The U.S. Embassy continues to operate in Iraq, although the mandatory departure order for non-essential U.S. government personnel remains in effect.

World.title: Starlink officially launches satellite internet service in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Starlink officially launched its satellite internet service in Iraq on Wednesday, expanding high-speed broadband access across the country following the completion of licensing procedures with Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

The announcement was confirmed by CMC Chairman Balegh Abu Kalal, who declared the service officially operational.

“With God’s blessing, Starlink has officially launched in Iraq,” Abu Kalal said in a statement issued by the commission.

At the same time, Starlink updated its official service map, listing Iraq among the countries where its high-speed satellite internet service is now available.

Launch follows licensing agreement

The commercial launch comes just weeks after Iraqi authorities finalized Starlink’s operating license.

Earlier this month, Abu Kalal revealed that the licensing agreement and related security arrangements were signed inside Iraq before the government’s visit to Washington, describing the move as a step to safeguard Iraq’s digital sovereignty.

According to the CMC, the agreement requires Starlink to comply with Iraqi laws and security regulations, including cooperation with relevant authorities on licensed devices and regulatory requirements.

Government highlights security safeguards

Officials have previously said the licensing framework gives Iraqi authorities oversight of the service through agreements reached with the company and national security institutions.

The CMC also stated that Starlink agreed to comply with decisions issued by Iraq’s competent authorities, including regulations governing telecommunications services.

In addition, officials have said the agreement is intended to address the widespread use of unlicensed Starlink terminals already operating in Iraq.

Subscription prices and revenue sharing

According to previous statements by Abu Kalal, monthly subscription fees are expected to range between IQD 75,000 and IQD 150,000, depending on the service package.

The agreement also provides Iraq with a share of the company’s revenues, including an 8% direct contribution, an additional 1% universal service fee, and a 15% corporate tax applicable to telecommunications companies.

Experts see boost for digital connectivity

Technology experts have welcomed the launch, saying satellite internet could significantly improve connectivity in underserved and remote areas.

Communications infrastructure expert Redha Khudair Elias previously said Starlink plans to establish seven ground stations around Baghdad, allowing Iraqi authorities to oversee the service under the agreed regulatory framework.

Meanwhile, technology specialist Nawras Aref has urged government institutions to continue strengthening their cybersecurity capabilities to keep pace with rapidly evolving communications technologies.

Long path to market

Starlink’s entry into Iraq follows months of negotiations between Iraqi authorities and the company.

The process began under the previous government, which hosted a SpaceX delegation in December 2025 to discuss licensing for satellite internet services.

More recently, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi met Starlink executives during his visit to Washington, where Iraqi officials also signed the company’s final operating license.

The launch represents one of Iraq’s most significant telecommunications developments in recent years, with officials aiming to expand internet access while maintaining regulatory oversight of satellite-based communications.

World.title: PMF says 20 members killed, 32 injured in Joint US-Saudi airstrikes across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) on Wednesday announced that at least 20 of its members were killed and 32 others wounded in what it described as joint U.S.-Saudi airstrikes targeting its facilities across several Iraqi provinces.

In a statement, the PMF said the casualty figures remain preliminary, adding that search and damage assessment operations are still underway and the toll could rise.

According to the statement, the strikes hit official PMF headquarters in Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, and Diyala. The organization said the attacks also caused varying degrees of damage to military facilities, vehicles, and equipment stationed at the targeted sites.

Furthermore, the PMF described the operation as a “joint U.S.-Saudi aggression,” accusing both countries of carrying out coordinated attacks against its positions.

The PMF stressed that specialized committees continue to assess the extent of the damage and verify information from the affected locations.

As a result, it said the announced death toll of 20 members and 32 wounded represents an initial estimate that may increase as field investigations and rescue efforts continue.

The group added that comprehensive reports will be released once the assessment process is completed.

The PMF statement came hours after the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that American and Saudi forces had carried out coordinated airstrikes against what it described as Iran-backed militia positions across Iraq.

Saudi Arabia later confirmed its participation in the operation, saying the strikes targeted groups linked to recent drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities while emphasizing that the Kingdom does not seek further escalation.

Iraqi authorities have yet to issue a comprehensive official assessment of the reported casualties or the full impact of the strikes.

World.title: Iraqi PM cancels trip to Saudi Arabia amid security escalation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi canceled on Wednesday his trip to Saudi Arabia, which was scheduled for Thursday.

The step took place after major regional security escalations earlier in the day. The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites in several Iraqi provinces.

The airstrikes come in response to repeated drone assaults on Saudi Arabia’s eastern oil facilities over the past few days.

Riyadh said earlier that the drone attacks were launched by Iran-backed militias inside Iraq.

An Iraqi government source told Shafaq News that all preparations for al-Zaidi’s visit to Saudi Arabia had been suspended due to the fast-paced security developments.

According to reports, al-Zaidi was scheduled to discuss the deadline set by the government on September 30 to disarm unauthorized armed organizations.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was expected to publicly support Iraq’s efforts to impose governmental control on weaponry.

Al-Zaidi wanted to personally reassure Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that Iraqi land will not be used to attack neighboring countries.

Before the trip was canceled, al-Zaidi directed Iraq’s security services to launch an official investigation into the drone claims. However, the US-Saudi strikes prompted the suspension of diplomatic discussions.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes in Iraq kill 20 Iran-backed fighters
World.content:
Baghdad — US-Saudi strikes on Iraq on Wednesday killed at least 20 members of a former paramilitary alliance that includes pro-Iran groups, the alliance said.

The Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), an alliance of former paramilitary groups and factions now integrated into the Iraqi armed forces, said at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll” following the US-Saudi strikes on its bases in seven provinces.

World.title: Search for survivors after powerful Japan quake kills 13
World.content:
Kumamoto – Rescuers battled through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall Wednesday searching for any trapped survivors after a big earthquake killed at least 13 people.

A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people.

The tremor on the island of Kyushu caused widespread damage, flattening homes, triggering fires and leaving left tens of thousands of residents without power and water.

Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.

“The cause is still being investigated, but it’s likely that gas caused it,” fellow Aeon executive Keiji Ohno told a news conference where he and others bowed in apology.

Five people were also confirmed killed and four others were unaccounted for at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, where part of a red-and-white smokestack collapsed, a government official told AFP.

“Extensive damage has been confirmed, including casualties, collapsed buildings, fires and damage to roads,” Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in Tokyo as she announced 13 fatalities, describing a “race against time” to help those affected.

Government spokesman Minoru Kihara said that as of early Wednesday more than 9,000 people had sought refuge in 506 shelters in three regions of Kyushu island.

Around 130 police, 450 firefighters and 170 military personnel were involved in the rescue operation at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto, he said.

Some stunned locals said the quake was the biggest they had felt in their lifetimes, measuring at the top of Japan’s seven-level shindo scale of shakiness.

“It was the strongest quake I ever experienced,” Kanzo Matsumoto, 73, the operator of a luxury onsen hot spring inn in Yatsushiro, told AFP.

“I’m not sure if (the region) will be able to recover from the damage.”

– ‘Then an explosion’ –

Tokito Kitagawa, 21, pulled over at a convenience store when the quake struck as he was travelling in Kumamoto on his motorcycle.

“There was a sudden big noise,” Kitagawa told AFP. “I couldn’t stay standing. I had to crouch down. Then all the cup noodles fell all over me on the floor.”

One user on X who said that they worked inside the mall recounted the moments after the quake hit.

The user with the handle Palan said staff had guided customers outside and then some employees went back to get their belongings.

“Since there didn’t seem to be any smoke inside the premises from what we could see, we felt reassured,” they said. “Then an explosion occurred.”

Footage from inside the mall showed rescue workers in orange overalls and white helmets picking their way through a mass of twisted steel, dangling cables and chunks of ceiling.

Initial reports had said that as many as 20 to 30 people were trapped inside.

Some 31,200 households and facilities still had no power on Wednesday morning, while 84,000 homes were suffering water disruptions, officials said.

TV footage showed people queueing for petrol and drinking water.

– Trains suspended –

The powerful tremor, which struck at 4:27 pm (0727 GMT) on Tuesday, knocked over a cargo train, flattened a traditional “torii” gateway and cracked roads, making many impassable.

High-speed shinkansen trains mostly remained suspended on Wednesday.

Footage also showed parts of a wall at the centuries-old Kumamoto Castle collapsing.

The US Geological Survey measured the quake at 6.8, lower than Japan’s reading of 7.1.

Japan is one of the world’s most seismically active countries, sitting on top of four major tectonic plates along the western edge of the Pacific “Ring of Fire”.

Kumamoto was hit by two devastating earthquakes in 2016, which killed 273 people and injured more than 2,800.

The archipelago, home to around 125 million people, typically experiences hundreds of jolts every year and accounts for about 18 percent of the world’s earthquakes.

The vast majority are mild, although the damage they cause varies according to their location and the depth below the Earth’s surface at which they strike.

Japan is haunted by the memory of a massive 9.0-magnitude undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.

World.title: Iraq seeks to raise trade exchange with Turkey to $30 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Trade Minister Mustafa al-Ani confirmed on Tuesday that the government plans to increase trade exchange with Turkey to $30 billion.

Al-Ani’s remarks followed his meeting with Turkish Trade Minister Omer Bolat in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on the sidelines of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s official visit to Turkey, according to a statement cited by the state-run news agency (INA).

During the meeting, the two sides confirmed their commitment to strengthening Iraq-Turkey trade and economic relations, broadening the scope of cooperation, and boosting joint investments to transform the two countries’ strategic partnership into tangible economic results serving their common interests.

The meeting focused on strategies to increase bilateral commerce to $30 billion, initiatives to support the Development Road project, and approaches to enhance transportation and customs cooperation.

The two sides also discussed the ongoing preparations for the third meeting of the Iraqi-Turkish Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO III) in the fourth quarter of this year, which will strengthen the economic partnership and open up new avenues for trade and investment cooperation.

Bolat said earlier that Turkish exports to Iraq hit $8.7 billion in the first nine months of 2025, while trade between the two countries was almost $12 billion.

Turkish enterprises have undertaken 1,145 projects in Iraq, totaling $36.6 billion. This amount represents approximately 6.7 percent of their entire global project portfolio, positioning Iraq as the third-largest market for Turkish contractors worldwide.

World.title: Karnataka bags lion’s share of electronics startup fund; 90 of 128 firms based in state
World.content:
Karnataka bags lionâs share of electronics startup fund; 90 of 128 firms based in state

NEW DELHI: Karnataka has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the Centreâs Electronics Development Fund (EDF), accounting for 90 of the 128 companies backed under the scheme and nearly two-thirds of the total investment made by its associated venture funds.The eight âdaughter fundsâ supported by EDF invested Rs 1,335.77 crore in 128 startups and companies as of June 30, the electronics and information technology ministry told Lok Sabha on Wednesday. Of these, 77 firms were working in electronics system design and manufacturing and 51 in information technology.Bengaluru alone accounted for 89 companies â 56 in electronics manufacturing and 33 in IT â while one company was based in Belagavi. Together, Karnataka-based firms received Rs 854.54 crore, or about 64% of the total investment.Telangana was a distant second, with seven Hyderabad-based companies receiving Rs 129.97 crore. Eight companies in Mumbai and Pune received Rs 142.48 crore, while six Delhi firms were allotted Rs 99.2 crore. Five Chennai companies received Rs 62.24 crore.The remaining investments went to companies in Haryana, Kerala, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.No company from Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu figured among the beneficiaries, according to the state-wise data submitted in Parliament.EDF was established as a âfund of fundsâ, with the government investing Rs 257.77 crore in eight professionally managed, Sebi-registered venture funds. These funds subsequently deployed more than five times that amount in technology companies. The supported firms have collectively raised around Rs 22,553.82 crore and created or acquired 373 intellectual-property assets, the ministry said.Companies were selected on the basis of their innovation potential, indigenous technology development, capacity to create intellectual property, the technical strength of their founding teams and the commercial scalability of their business models.Canbank Venture Capital Fund Ltd manages EDF, while the electronics ministry is its anchor investor. The fund completed its investment phase in February 2024 and is now in the divestment phase. Its daughter funds continue to monitor the operational performance, market growth and technological progress of the companies they backed.

World.title: 'Kuchu-puchu', 'delulu', 'clock it': Decoding the GenZ vocabulary now echoing in Parliament
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

âThe Leader of the Opposition had gone '

MIA

'. '

FOMO

' perhaps explains why he eventually went and sat outside the Prime Minister's residence.â

These are the words of 69-year old Union minister Jitendra SIngh, who was addressing the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.

Until recently, these words belonged to Instagram comment sections, meme pages, K-pop fan communities and WhatsApp chats.

This week, however, they echoed through the halls of Parliament.

During the Monsoon session, MPs infused their speeches with Gen Z slang and internet catchphrases while taking on political rivals, discussing governance and framing arguments around issues ranging from education to development.

BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj, while defending the Centre's policies, urged the Opposition to "

clock it

" â a Gen Z phrase meaning to recognise or acknowledge something.

"Where Congress created a policy vacuum, Modi clocked it, if I may borrow the language of Gen Z, and created a solution. All the Opposition did was chase political opportunism," she said, explicitly acknowledging that she was borrowing from the vocabulary of younger generations.

BJPâs Tejasvi Surya reached for another popular internet expression, calling the Opposition "

delulu

" â shorthand for "delusional" â suggesting its criticism of the government was detached from reality.





Not to be left behind, Congress MP Deepender Hooda, during debate on anti-paper leak in Lok Sabha, slipped in â

Kuchu Puchu

â and viral internet catchphrase â

Vasteguna Huiya

â in a swipe at Centre. â

Aaj mera birthday hai toh please kuchu-puchu isteefa de do naaa

(Today is my birthday, so please resign cutie pie)," he remarked, giving example of slogans at the recent student protests.

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Eknath Shinde labelled the Opposition as suffering from "

FOMO

" â the "Fear of Missing Out" â and even described it as "

MIA

" (Missing in Action), implying that the Opposition was scrambling to remain politically relevant after missing key opportunities.

It was an unusual moment.

As Hooda put it, the GenZ with Bhagat Singhâs slogan of âInquilab Zindabadâ, turned it into âVastaguna huiyaâ when they protested against the government.

Parliament, traditionally associated with constitutional language, Hindi idioms and literary references, suddenly sounded like an Instagram comment thread.

What these words mean and where they come from

The internet has a way of making words travel across continents, cultures and generations.

Many expressions that now dominate Gen Z conversations were born in niche online communities long before they entered mainstream discourse.

Clock It

Unlike many internet expressions, "clock it" has a much older cultural lineage. The phrase traces its roots to African-American and LGBTQ+ ballroom culture in the United States, where "to clock" someone meant to notice, identify or call out somethingâoften a flaw or inconsistency.

Popularised through drag culture and shows such as

RuPaul's Drag Race

, the expression later migrated to TikTok and Instagram, where Gen Z adopted it to mean "spot the truth" or "call it as it is".

Vasteguna Huiya

The phrase traces its roots to the viral meme "Can I get a Hoya?", in which a teenager shouted the line in an exaggerated tone. In India, content creators gave the meme a local twist by replacing the original phrase with the nonsensical-sounding "Vasteguna Huiya".

The humour lay not in the words themselvesâthey have no literal meaningâbut in the confused reactions they elicited. From there, the phrase spread rapidly across Instagram memes, reels and comment sections before making its way into the CJP student protests.

Kuchu Puchu

"Kuchu Puchu" does not have a single, traceable origin like "delulu" or "FOMO". Instead, it evolved organically from baby talk, a simplified, affectionate style of speech used by parents, grandparents and couples across many Indian languages.

The phrase is believed to be a playful variation of words like "kuchi kuchi," "guchu puchu," "kuchi poo," and similar rhyming expressions that mimic the sounds babies make. Such reduplicative words are common in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and several other Indian languages, where they are used as terms of endearment for children, pets or romantic partners.

In recent years, "kuchu puchu" was revived and popularised by Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and meme pages, where it took on a new, often sarcastic meaning.

Calling someone "kuchu puchu" can imply that they are overly pampered, babied, innocent or treated with excessive affection.

Its popularity surged during the CJP-led student protests, where protesters and social media users used "kuchu puchu" satirically to poke fun at political leaders and institutions.

FOMO

Unlike most Gen Z slang, FOMO predates social media. The acronym, standing for "Fear of Missing Out", entered popular vocabulary in the early 2000s as psychologists and marketers described the anxiety people felt when they believed others were enjoying experiences they were not part of.

Instagram amplified the phenomenon, turning FOMO into one of the defining emotions of the social media age. Today, the term is used far beyond personal lifeâto describe everything from investment trends to political strategy.

MIA

Originally a military abbreviation for "Missing in Action", MIA has been repurposed by internet users to describe people who suddenly disappear from conversations, social media or public life.

Delulu

Perhaps the most recognisable Gen Z word today, "delulu" is a shortened version of "delusional". It first gained popularity within K-pop fandoms, where devoted fans jokingly described unrealistic fantasiesâsuch as believing their favourite idol secretly loved themâas being "delulu".

Over time, the term evolved beyond fandom culture to describe anyone perceived as wildly optimistic or disconnected from reality.

Today, it has become a staple of political banter, where opponents routinely accuse each other of being "delulu".

Why Gen Z language matters

The timing of Parliament's linguistic makeover is not accidental.

The recent protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over NEET examination paper leaks were organised as much on Instagram and X as they were on the streets. Protesters used memes, short-form videos, viral hashtags and internet humour to mobilise students and simplify complex issues around examination reforms.

For many young Indians, politics is now consumed through Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and meme pages rather than lengthy parliamentary speeches or television debates. Viral clips often carry more influence than hour-long discussions.

Taking notice of the same after massive protests, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also advised his Cabinet to engage with the youth on Instagram through reels and interactive sessions.

"Young people are just on Instagram. This is a potential segment of citizens that we all need to connect with," he said.

India's demographic profile makes this shift even more significant. With one of the world's youngest populations and millions of first-time voters entering the electorate every election cycle, speaking the language of youth has become a political strategy as much as a communication style.

Parliament has always borrowed popular language

Although Gen Z slangs in Parliament may sound dramatic, Parliament has always reflected the language of its times.

In the early decades after Independence, speeches frequently quoted verses from the

Bhagavad Gita

, couplets by poets like Mirza Ghalib, Allama Iqbal. Hindi literary works were seen as a mark of oratorical skill.

Long before MPs began saying "delulu" or "clock it", Parliament had embraced the language of popular culture. Bollywood dialogues have long been used to simplify political arguments, inject humour and produce memorable sound bites.

Rahul Gandhi's dig at GST by calling it "Gabbar Singh Tax" transformed a complex debate on GST into a phrase instantly understood across India, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi invoked the character "Mausi" from the Sholay to mock the Congress party during his address in Parliament on July 2, 2024. He teased the opposition over their electoral defeat by mimicking a dialogue: "

Arey Mausi, teesri baar toh haare hain, par moral victory toh hai na!

" (Oh Mausi, we have lost for the third time too, but it's a moral victory, right?).

In another instance, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut brought DDLJâs iconic dialogue â

Ja Simran, jeele apni zindagi

â to life while addressing womenâs reservation bill in Lok Sabha.

Cricket metaphors soon followed, with terms like "hitting a six", "playing on the back foot" or being "clean bowled" by the Opposition. Finance ministers have described Budgets as "innings", while election victories and defeats have routinely been framed as cricket matches.

In many ways, Gen Z slang is simply the latest chapter in this evolution. Parliament has never existed in a linguistic vacuum; it has always absorbed the language spoken beyond its walls.

Language keeps evolving

Every generation believes the next one's vocabulary sounds strange.

Words like "cool", "awesome", "dude" and "LOL" were once dismissed as youthful fads before becoming mainstream. Today's internet lexicon follows the same trajectory.

Many Gen Z expressions have travelled remarkable distancesâfrom Korean pop fandoms to American drag culture, from gaming communities to TikTok trendsâbefore landing in Indian political discourse. Their journey illustrates how digital platforms have accelerated the movement of language across borders and cultures.

Not every slang term will survive. Internet vocabulary evolves at dizzying speed, with new words replacing old ones every few months.

But some expressions inevitably escape their online origins to become part of everyday speech.

When lawmakers adopt them, it signals that these words have crossed into the mainstream.

When Bansuri Swaraj paused to say, "if I may borrow the language of Gen Z", she acknowledged something larger than a passing linguistic trend.

Politics is no longer communicated solely through ideological speeches or parliamentary rhetoric.

It increasingly competes in the same digital ecosystem as influencers, meme pages and viral videos, where relatability often matters as much as reasoned argument.

Whether that makes parliamentary debate more accessible or more performative remains open to debate. But one thing is clear: as India's politics becomes increasingly digital, the House is learning to speak not just to Gen Z, but increasingly like Gen Z.

World.title: Times Samman Dehradun 2026: A tribute to brave hearts from Sainya Bhoomi
World.content:
Uttarakhand has emerged as a preferred destination for defence personnel, with institutions like IMA, RIMC, etc., and a growing creative ecosystem. What gives Uttarakhand a special status is its glory as a state of defence, holding a fundamental value for national defence.

The Times Group proudly presented âTimes Samman 2026 â A Tribute to Indiaâs Defence Forces & Importance of AI in Drone Technologyâ, an initiative dedicated to honouring the courage, sacrifice, and legacy of Indiaâs armed forces. The grand felicitation ceremony was hosted in June 2026 in Dehradun, and brought together distinguished dignitaries, defence personnel, gallantry awardees, industry leaders, and young aspirants.

Families of 32 brave hearts who sacrificed their lives in the line of duty from Uttarakhand were felicitated at a special ceremony organised by the Optimal Media Solutions (OMS) division of Times of India on Monday evening, honouring the stateâs deep-rooted legacy of military service.

As the event was centred around the felicitation of fallen heroes from Uttarakhand, Chief Guest, in his address, said that Uttarakhand plays a significant role in defence services and that the people of the state have made immense contributions to the armed forces.

He highlighted prominent personalities from Uttarakhand who hold key posts such as CDS and NSA, and acknowledged the deep-rooted devotion of the people towards the armed forces, a sentiment that inspired PM Narendra Modi to address the Himalayan state as âSainya Bhoomi.

â

The event was attended by families of the fallen heroes and ex-servicemen. It commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by Uttarakhand Assembly Speaker, Ritu Khanduri Bhushan and Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology Director General Durgesh Pant.

Speaker Ritu Khanduri Bhushan praised the initiative, noting that virtually every family in the state has contributed members to the defence forces, spanning all ranks from jawans to the Chief of Defence Staff. She also recalled the discipline of her late father, Major General B. C. Khanduri, and highlighted Uttarakhandâs identity as a land of brave hearts who consistently lead from the front.

Soldier Welfare Minister, Ganesh Joshi referred to Uttarakhand as âSainya Bhoomiâ(Land of Soldiers) due to its massive contribution to the armed forces.

âI understand the hardships faced by soldiers as well as their families. We salute their contribution to safeguarding the country,â Joshi said.

Panel Discussion: Implementation of AI in defence technology



The session was moderated by Saurabh Saxena, a tech professional, ecosystem builder, and Managing Partner, Gorkha Ventures.

Col. Kothiyal, spoke about not losing sight of human intelligence in the age of AI, and emphasized the need to keep investing in human capital despite the AI wave.

Prof. Durgesh Pant stressed the importance of building a complete indigenous tech infrastructure. âWe can never be truly safe if our entire country runs on international infra which can be disrupted at any time.â

Ashish Kumar Upadhyay (DGM, ITDA) talked about building security at every layer and training young engineers in the importance of building safeguards within government systems.

Shubham Pandey, an AI Expert, emphasised the importance of training local talent while building an ecosystem that promotes reverse migration, inviting locals who had moved out seeking opportunities.

The event was supported by Centurion Defence Academy as the Presenting Sponsor, MDDA Dehradun as the Powered By Partner, Hamdard as the Wellness Partner, Yugen Infra as the Luxury Golf Resort Living Township Partner, UCOST Dehradun as the Technology Partner, Trust Toyota as the Auto Partner, Saigrace Academy International as the Education Partner, and Quantum University and IMS Unison University as Associate Partners.

World.title: Vande Mataram Bill 2026 explained: What changes and what punishment it proposes
World.content:
The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, paving the way for Vande Mataram to receive the same statutory protection.

The amendment is intended to place National Song Vande Mataram on the same legal footing as

with respect to protection against insult or disruption.

During a debate in the Rajya Sabha, MoS for home affairs Nityanand Rai said the amendment was "not merely a legislative change" but reflected the country's commitment to "the soul of India, national consciousness, cultural heritage, and the ideals of the freedom struggle."

What does the current law say?

The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 currently provides statutory protection to the National Flag, the Constitution of India, and the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana.

Under Section 3of the Act, it is a punishable offence to intentionally prevent the singing of the National Anthem or disturb an assembly engaged in its rendition. Such offences are punishable withimprisonment for up to three years, a fine, or both.





What changes does the Bill propose?

The amendment seeks to extend the legal protections currently available to the National Anthem to Vande Mataram. If enacted into law, deliberately insulting the National Song, intentionally preventing its singing, or disrupting an assembly engaged in singing it would become punishable offences.

These acts would attract the same penalty as similar offences involving the National Anthem under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, with punishment of up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both.

The Rajya Sabha has passed the Bill, but it must complete the remaining constitutional process before becoming law, including any remaining parliamentary approval, if applicable, and receiving the President's assent.

Why was the amendment introduced?

The song, composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, played a significant role in India's freedom struggle. At the Constituent Assembly meeting held on January 24, 1950, its President, Dr Rajendra Prasad, stated that Vande Mataram, which had played a historic role in the freedom movement, "shall be honoured equally with Jana Gana Mana" and accorded equal respect, even as Jana Gana Mana was adopted as the national anthem.

Despite this recognition, Vande Mataram did not enjoyed the same statutory protection under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, a gap the proposed amendment seeks to address.

The government says the amendment seeks to remove this distinction by extending identical legal safeguards.

World.title: Bihar transgender welfare board approves proposal to build temple dedicated to PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board on Wednesday approved a proposal to construct a temple dedicated to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with a board member saying the prime minister had given the transgender community "respect and rights".

The proposal was moved by board member Ranjan Singh during the maiden meeting of the board, which functions under the Bihar government's Social Welfare Department.

"Since the transgender community in Bihar does not have a temple of its own, I proposed to build a temple for Narendra Modi because he gave us respect and rights. The proposal received the support of all members and was approved by the board," Singh told PTI.

The Bihar government constituted the Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board in August last year to safeguard the rights of the transgender community and undertake measures for its social development and empowerment.

According to Singh, Wednesday's meeting was the first gathering of the board after the implementation of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

"Today's meeting marked the first gathering of the Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board following the enactment of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, which provided the transgender community with institutional representation in the state secretariat," Singh said.

World.title: Over 1 lakh schools run with just one teacher; Andhra tops list with 16,357
World.content:
NEW DELHI: More than one lakh schools across India are functioning with a single teacher, with Andhra Pradesh alone accounting for over 16,000, government data has revealed, highlighting severe deployment gaps despite the countryâs overall pupil-teacher ratio remaining within national norms.

According to UDISE+ data for 2025-26, India has 1,00,843 single-teacher schools across all management categories. Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools â more than 16% of the national total â followed by Jharkhand with 9,827 and Maharashtra with 9,269.

Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, Uttar Pradesh 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Together, the seven states account for nearly 65% of all schools in the country operating with only one teacher.

The problem is spread across regions rather than being confined to poorer or geographically difficult states. Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159. Himachal Pradesh has 3,128, Uttarakhand 2,655 and Chhattisgarh 2,461.

At the other end, Kerala reported 67 single-teacher schools, Nagaland 35, Sikkim 31, Ladakh 28, Delhi seven and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands one.

The figures were provided by minister of state for education Jayant Chaudhary in response to a Rajya Sabha question on teacher vacancies.





While the question sought data specifically for government schools, the annexure on single-teacher institutions covers schools under all managements.

The ministry did not provide state-wise sanctioned posts or vacancies, saying recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers were handled by state governments and Union Territory administrations. It attributed vacancies to retirement, resignation, creation of posts, staff rationalisation and changing enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts.

The Centre said states were regularly advised to fill posts through transparent, merit-based recruitment and use technology for forecasting teacher requirements. Financial support was also provided under Samagra Shiksha to maintain prescribed pupil-teacher ratios.

The ministry cited national pupil-teacher ratios of 19 at the primary level, 17 at upper primary, 15 at secondary and 23 at higher secondary â all within the limits envisaged under the National Education Policy. However, the single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability.

World.title: 'No abnormality found in fuel control switch': Government on Air India Boeing 787 crash
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday said no abnormality has been found in the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the Air India Boeing 787 Dreamliner that crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad on June 12 last year killing 260 people on board and on the ground.

Civil aviation state minister Murlidhar Mohol informed the Rajya Sabha that the fuel control switch was examined at the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level in Seattle as part of continued airworthiness checks ordered by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Reuters repeorted.

A detailed examination of the fuel control switch, including the structural integrity of its locking detents, found 'no abnormality', Mohol said in his response to questions raised by Congress MP Jebi Mather Hisham.

However, the examination of the complete thrust control module is still underway at the OEM facility in Seattle.

"Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), as part of continued airworthiness, directed Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level testing of Fuel Control Switch Locking Mechanism in Seattle. Detailed examination of Fuel Control Switch including structural integrity of Fuel Control Switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed.





However, further inspection of complete 'Thrust Control Module' at OEM facility is underway," Mohol write in his written reply.

What the government said about the AI-171 probe

The government also rejected suggestions that the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has delayed its final report into the crash.

In her Rajya Sabha question, Mather had asked the government to state the reasons for the delay in releasing the final report more than a year after the crash, whether pilot conduct was among the factors being examined and whether the government would announce a public release date for the complete report.

Responding to these questions, Mohol said there was 'no delay' in the investigation and explained that major accident investigations cannot be completed according to a fixed timeline.

"There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process involving multiple variables," he said in the written reply.

The minister said the investigation remains under way and that all possible causes and contributing factors are being examined.

"All probable causes and contributing factors leading to the accident are being investigated," Mohol said.

The government said the final investigation report, containing all the findings of the probe, would be made public and published on the AAIB website once the investigation is complete.

Air India flight AI-171, which was headed to London, crashed shortly after taking off from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025.

The Boeing 787 struck a medical college hostel complex soon after take-off. The crash killed 241 people on board and 19 people on the ground, while one passenger survived.

The disaster became one of India's deadliest aviation accidents in recent years and triggered a detailed investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash.

Fuel switches moved to 'CUTOFF' after take-off

A preliminary investigation report released last year found that the fuel control switches of both engines moved from 'RUN' to 'CUTOFF' shortly after take-off, cutting the fuel supply and causing both engines to shut down.

A cockpit recording also captured a brief exchange between the pilots in which one pilot appeared to ask the other why the switches had been moved, while the other denied doing so. The finding raised questions about whether the switches had been moved by a pilot or whether a technical issue could have been responsible.

The government has not provided a specific date for publication of the final AAIB report.

Mohol said the investigation was still progressing and that the report would be released only after the inquiry is completed. The government has maintained that the investigation will cover all probable causes and contributing factors.

World.title: 'Citizens have every right to demand answers': CJP responds to Delhi Police notice to X over 'derogatory content'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (

) on Wednesday criticised a

notice to social media platform X seeking the removal of allegedly derogatory and defamatory content targeting constitutional authorities, saying citizens have the right to question elected representatives and demand accountability.

In a post on X, the CJP said criticism of public officials should not be treated as a criminal act and argued that citizens have a right to raise questions about the functioning of the government.

"Since when is an elected representative above questioning? In a functioning democracy, citizens have every right to demand answers and accountability from their PM. By treating online criticism as a criminal offense and a threat to "public order", the state machinery is sending a chilling message: the Prime Minister is beyond the reach of public scrutiny," CJP wrote in a post on X.

The CJP's remarks came after Delhi Police wrote to social media platform X seeking the removal of content allegedly containing 'derogatory, malicious and defamatory content' targeting constitutional authorities.

In its notice, the Delhi Police asked X to 'immediately delete/remove' the alleged post or video and provide complete details of the account that uploaded the content. The information sought includes the user's full name, address, contact number and email ID.





The police also sought the account's login and logout details, along with corresponding timestamps and any other information that could assist the investigation.

X has also been asked to preserve all data related to the post or video for the ongoing probe and provide a certificate under Section 63(4) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).

The latest notice comes days after Delhi Police directed multiple social media platforms to remove posts and videos containing offensive and abusive remarks against

that were allegedly uploaded during student protests at Jantar Mantar and the violence linked to the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march.

According to police officials, several posts containing abusive language targeting the Prime Minister surfaced across social media platforms during the protests and subsequent clashes in the national capital.

Delhi Police's social media monitoring team has been scanning online platforms for objectionable content linked to the protests. Officials said notices are being issued to social media intermediaries whenever such posts are identified.

Police said several posts and videos containing abusive remarks against the Prime Minister have already been removed following such notices.

The monitoring exercise is continuing, with cyber and social media teams keeping track of online activity linked to the protests and identifying content that may violate applicable rules.

The party's statement comes amid heightened political tensions following the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march, during which students protesting alleged irregularities in NEET and CBSE examinations clashed with security personnel while marching from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament.

The protests also triggered a wider political dispute over alleged police action against students and the registration of cases against protesters.

The Supreme Court has separately been hearing pleas concerning alleged police excesses during the protests. The court has stressed the constitutional protection of peaceful protest while also noting that violence and attacks on police personnel cannot be permitted.

World.title: EVMs used in Kolathur constituency being verified after M.K. Stalin’s petition to Election Commission
World.content:
The checking and verification of the burnt memory and microcontroller of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) used in 14 polling booths in the Kolathur constituency during the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election was undertaken on Wednesday (July 29, 2026) following a petition filed by defeated DMK candidate and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin before the Election Commission of India (ECI).

Mr. Stalin lost the constituency to Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) candidate V.S. Babu by a margin of 8,795 votes.

Acting on Mr. Stalin’s representation, Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran, who is also the District Election Officer, wrote to the DMK leader requesting him or his authorised representative to be present during the verification process. Mr. Stalin is being represented by senior advocate N.R. Elango. The verification is being carried out at Chintadripet.

In his petition, the DMK candidate alleged that the votes expected to have been polled in his favour were not recorded in these 14 polling booths.

Verification in other districts

Mr. Sameeran said similar checking and verification of EVMs are being conducted in a few other districts including Kancheepuram, Virudhunagar, and Sivaganga. He said the facility was available to candidates who had secured one of the top three positions in a constituency, with verification being carried out for up to 5% of the EVMs used.

“We are checking and verifying the EVMs used in 14 polling stations selected by the candidate in the Kolathur constituency. The exercise will be carried out in two phases. In the first phase, the ballot unit, control unit, and VVPAT of two polling stations will be verified. The authentication is being carried out under the supervision of engineers from Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL),” he said.

Mr. Sameeran said the representatives of the candidates were shown the votes polled by each candidate as recorded in the burnt memory, and no discrepancies had been found.

“In the second phase, a mock poll involving a minimum of 500 votes and a maximum of 1,400 votes will be conducted. The entire exercise is intended to verify the authenticity of the EVMs,” he said.

The checking and verification process will continue for seven days.

World.title: Over 672 kg ganja, 23 tonnes of gutkha seized in West Zone districts in three months
World.content:
In a major crackdown on narcotics and prohibited tobacco products, the police seized 672.893 kg of ganja and 23.53 tonnes of gutkha from the eight West Zone districts in the past three months.

A total of 16,479 tablets of different prescription drugs, 586 gm of methamphetamine, 360 ml of cannabis oil, 9.86 kg of cannabis-infused toffees, 48 stamps of lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), five cannabis plants, 130 gm of magic mushroom and 80 gm of cocaine were also seized during the police action from May 1 to July 25.

In July alone, 325.69 kg of ganja and 12.11 tonnes of prohibited tobacco products were seized from the eight districts, namely Coimbatore, the Nilgiris, Tiruppur, Erode, Salem, Namakkal, Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri.

Special drives and simultaneous action conducted under the supervision of R.V. Ramya Bharathi, Inspector General of Police (West Zone) in the eight districts have crippled the drug trafficking and retail networks, according to officials involved in the operations.

Meanwhile, the police have also taken serious note of the growing availability of synthetic drugs such as methamphetamine, LSD and cocaine in the region.

Officials added that invoking the Goondas Act and freezing of bank accounts are among other actions being taken against drug offenders in the West Zone.

World.title: Yadgir: Lokayukta traps Health Department assistant for accepting ₹20,000 bribe via UPI
World.content:
The Karnataka Lokayukta Police have trapped an official of the District Health and Family Welfare Department in Yadgir for allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹20,000 through a UPI transaction.

According to a press release issued by the Lokayukta Police, the accused, Shrikant Bhavimani, Administrative and Programme Assistant, had allegedly demanded 20% commission from a beneficiary for releasing an incentive amount under the National Quality Assurance Programme (NQAP).

The complainant, Parameshwar Jamadar, 39, a farmer from Chitali village in Aland taluk of Kalaburagi district, alleged that although an incentive of ₹1,39,750 had been sanctioned to his account under the programme, the official demanded a commission for facilitating its release.

Following the complaint, the Karnataka Lokayukta Police registered a case (Crime No. 07/2026) under Section 7(b) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended in 2018), on July 27. During the trap operation, the accused allegedly accepted ₹20,000 through UPI and was caught by the Lokayukta team.

The operation was conducted under the guidance of Lokayukta Superintendent of Police Siddaraju C., led by Deputy Superintendent of Police J.H. Inamdar, with the participation of Police Inspector Siddaraya Balurgi and other Lokayukta personnel.

World.title: CPI(M) condemns Delhi Police action at party headquarters, seeks withdrawal of cases against student protesters
World.content:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) on Wednesday condemned the alleged police action at its central office in New Delhi and demanded the immediate withdrawal of cases registered against student leaders and protesters, alleging that the Union government was attempting to suppress democratic dissent.

The CPI(M) Vijayawada City Committee organised a protest in the city, with party leaders and activists staging a dharna against the alleged attempt by the Delhi Police to enter the party headquarters and arrest student leader Aishe Ghosh.

Addressing the protesters, CPI(M) State Secretariat member Ch. Babu Rao and State Committee member Donepudi Kashinath alleged that the Centre and the Delhi Police were targeting students and political activists who had taken part in peaceful protests. They described the alleged attempt to arrest Ms. Ghosh and the registration of criminal cases against student leaders as politically motivated and undemocratic.

The leaders alleged that the Centre was attempting to silence those questioning its policies by foisting false cases and resorting to arrests. They claimed that despite assurances that no action would be taken against peaceful protesters, the police had initiated coercive measures against students and their supporters.

Alleging excessive use of force against demonstrators in different parts of the country, the CPI(M) leaders urged the Union government to uphold the constitutional right to peaceful protest.

World.title: Heavy to very heavy rain forecast for nine Telangana districts for July 30
World.content:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange warning indicating heavy to very heavy rainfall in nine Telangana districts and a yellow alert indicating heavy rainfall in six districts for Thursday (July 30, 2026).

Nine Telangana districts under orange alert

According to IMDs latest bulletin, heavy to very heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Adilabad, Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Nirmal, Nizamabad, Vikarabad, Sangareddy, Medak and Kamareddy districts.

Six Telangana districts under yellow alert

Additionally, heavy rainfall is very likely to occur at isolated places in Jagtial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally and Mulugu districts.

Hyderabad weather forecast

Hyderabad city and its surrounding areas for the next 24 hours will see a generally cloudy sky. “Light to moderate rain or thundershowers are very likely to occur in the city. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 28℃ and 22℃ respectively,” as per the bulletin.
